title: bd_0ad-093.2 is a net throughput regression on stress scenario: AC #2 (cv::wait reduction) not met
description:
Superluminal A/B capture (HEAD vs parent baseline 7c21cfdfb6, combat_demo_huge, -autostart-speed=20, non-visual, 45s) shows bd_0ad-093.2 (TaskRef queue refactor + unconditional notify_all + adaptive spin-then-sleep) is a net-negative change on the saturated worker-pool case its own AC #2 targets:

Matched early window (2-17s, both captures, to avoid divergence-driven confound from unthrottled non-visual sim running different amounts of work per capture):
- Sim throughput (turns/sec): -5.1% (after does LESS work in the same wall time)
- cv::wait count per turn: +2.1% (rose, did not fall)
- cv::wait CPU per turn: -1.9% (negligible win)
- Spin CPU per turn (RunUntilDeath exclusive): +844% (0.00263ms -> 0.02483ms)
- Net synchronization CPU per turn: +23.2%

Full 45s capture (less trustworthy, inflated by state divergence as the slower build falls behind into cheaper/different game states): turns -12.5%, cv::wait count -11.4%, cv::wait CPU -17.8% -- these raw numbers look like a win but are fully explained by the after-build simply doing less total work, not by less synchronization overhead per unit of work.

Root cause: shares the same defect as bd_0ad-0rp (TaskManager.cpp:376 spin-decay gate is wrong -- gated on the shared m_HasWork observation rather than 'did this worker actually get a task', so workers that lose the PopTask race under contention never decay their spin budget). Under saturation the flag is legitimately true almost constantly, so the spin phase is entered on nearly every loop iteration; measured spin cost is dominated by std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now() (QPC) being called every single spin iteration (~20-25ns/call), not by cpu_Pause() itself.

Also: the parent commit ALREADY had a notify_all/notify_one batching heuristic in PushTasks (parent TaskManager.cpp:224-227) -- 093.2's 'always notify_all' change was not a meaningful behavior change vs baseline for this metric, which is why the notify-batching AC didn't move the needle either way.

Recommended fixes (perf-guru, unconfirmed by follow-up measurement since agent was measure-only): (1) fix the spin-decay gate (delete the spinFoundWork condition, decay unconditionally whenever the loop reaches that point without having executed a task) -- this is the same fix needed for bd_0ad-0rp; (2) hoist the clock read out of the inner spin loop, only check elapsed time every N pauses (e.g. 64) instead of every iteration; (3) consider whether the spin phase should be skipped/shortened specifically when PopTask fails due to contention (lost the race) vs genuine emptiness. If throughput doesn't recover after these fixes, recommend reverting the adaptive spin phase from WorkerThread::RunUntilDeath entirely -- the idle-case benefit measured for bd_0ad-0rp is only ~27ms/90s, nowhere near enough to justify a 5.1% throughput hit under load.

This blocks bd_0ad-093.2's AC #2 ('measured reduction in condition_variable::wait CPU time and count on the stress benchmark') -- that criterion is currently FAILED, not just unmeasured. bd_0ad-093.2 should not be considered fully closed until this is fixed and re-measured. Single run per config so far; deltas are far outside plausible noise per perf-guru but a second confirming run pair would be cheap insurance before committing to a fix.
close_reason: RESOLVED via clock-hoist fix (spin loop now checks elapsed time every 64 iterations instead of every iteration, removing the QueryPerformanceCounter call from the hot path). Re-measured (Superluminal A/B, combat_demo_huge, matched 2-17s window): throughput went from -5.1% vs baseline to +11.2% vs baseline -- not just recovered, better than the parent commit. cv::wait CPU per turn back near baseline (0.087ms vs 0.086ms baseline, was 0.109ms regressed). Caveat filed separately: this recovered throughput by spending MORE total sync CPU per turn (+55% vs baseline, 0.1376ms vs 0.0887ms) -- wall-clock win on a 24-core box where workers spin on otherwise-idle cores, but may invert on lower-core-count machines or under core contention from other subsystems. See follow-up bead for that tradeoff. AC #2 ('measured reduction in cv::wait CPU time and count') is separately NOT met (see bd_0ad-093.2 comment) -- wait count/CPU per turn never went below baseline across any of the three measured builds, since neither the original notify_all change nor this fix altered notify behavior, and the parent commit already had notify batching. That is a distinct, still-open question for bd_0ad-093.2's own AC, not blocking this bead's specific throughput-regression scope.

title: -replay produces no output (silent no-op); previously observed one-time segfault with -ooslog
description: Confirmed via QA investigation while validating bd_0ad-093.1/bd_0ad-093.8's determinism gate. Repro: cd binaries/system; ./pyrogenesis.exe -replay="<path to recorded commands.txt>" -logDir="<dir>" [-ooslog]. Expected: replay drives the recorded command stream through the simulation, producing normal logs (and -ooslog per-turn hash/state dumps under <logDir>/oos_logs/). Actual: process exits/completes with NO output whatsoever (no logs, no oos_logs dir) -- silent no-op, no error message. One earlier attempt with -ooslog produced a segfault (exit 139) instead, but this did not reliably reproduce across repeated attempts (may be non-deterministic, or may correlate with a specific input state -- not isolated). Confirmed PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to bd_0ad-093.1's code changes: reproduces identically on a clean stash of HEAD (CCmpObstruction/CCmpUnitMotionManager changes stashed out). commands.txt used was recorded via live -autostart="scenarios/combat_demo_huge" -autostart-nonvisual -autostart-speed=20 -autostart-max-turns=200, copied from the replays output dir. IMPACT: this is the core mechanism the bd_0ad-093.8 determinism-gate design depends on (replay a fixed recorded command stream to get wall-clock-pacing-immune, byte-comparable per-turn state hashes -- see bd_0ad-ea4 for why live -autostart-speed=20 runs cannot be used for this instead). With -replay non-functional, NO phase of the CPU-utilization epic can be rigorously determinism-validated via replay hash comparison until this is fixed. Also a standalone correctness/UX concern: replay is a player-facing feature (multiplayer OOS debugging, spectator replays) independent of this epic. NEXT STEPS: bisect why replay produces zero output -- check whether CReplayPlayer::Replay (source/ps/Replay.cpp) is even being reached (add temporary logging or check with a debugger), verify commands.txt format/location expectations haven't drifted (relative vs absolute path, VFS mount point, serialization_version-keyed subdirectory), and check recent branch history for anything touching replay/VFS path resolution (Windows VFS deny-read-sharing fix bd_0ad-dph, -logDir arg addition, -autostart-max-turns addition) that could have an unintended interaction with the -replay code path even though it wasn't the direct target of those changes.
close_reason: Fixed: source/main.cpp isNonVisualReplay path now initializes log dir, FileLogger, and required VFS mounts (mirroring InitVfs). Verified -replay produces logs/oos_logs correctly, no segfault. Debug+Release build clean, full test suite (494 tests) passes both configs. Follow-up for previously-observed non-reproducing -ooslog segfault filed separately.

title: Improve simulation CPU core utilization (motion parallelization + TaskManager overhaul)
description:
VTune (r009tr) + Superluminal (2026-09-09_12-43-09_pyrogenesis) capture analysis of headless combat_demo_huge stress run shows only 10.8% effective CPU utilization (2.6/24 cores). Main thread pegged ~92%, 23 worker threads ~13% each, ~20 cores idle at every instant. Root causes: (1) CCmpUnitMotionManager::Move/Push is 49% of every turn and 100% serial; (2) fork-join overhead in CCmpRangeManager::ExecuteActiveQueries is comparable to the work it parallelizes (1.1M condition-variable waits, 116.9s CPU in condition_variable::wait); (3) TaskManager has a single global mutex, full sleep/wake per task, no ParallelFor primitive; (4) oversubscription (23 workers + main = 24 threads on 24 cores) with no P/E-core awareness (1658s preemption wait); (5) only 2 sim systems use the task manager at all.

Full principal-engineer architecture blueprint (phases 0-6, file-level change lists, risk register, determinism gates) is recorded in session notes / conversation history dated 2026-09-09. This epic tracks the phased implementation. Scope is the simulation update loop only (capture had no renderer/AI active); expected realistic win ~2.5-3.5x turn throughput after phases 1-4b.
acceptance_criteria: All phases below closed; determinism/replay-hash gate green at each phase; benchmark shows measurable improvement in effective CPU utilization on combat_demo_huge stress scenario.

title: Precompute interface-presence mask in EntityData to kill per-candidate componentCache pointer chase in TestEntityQuery
description:
WHY: Post-fix Superluminal capture for bd_0ad-p8k (2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis, combat_demo_huge headless) shows that with CalcOwnerMask's cost eliminated from TestEntityQuery, the new dominant line inside TestEntityQuery is:

    const SEntityComponentCache* cache = entity.componentCache;
    if (!cache || static_cast<size_t>(q.interface) >= cache->numInterfaces || !cache->interfaces[q.interface])

This single dependent-load chain (EntityData -> componentCache -> interfaces[q.interface], two pointer hops off the hot per-candidate iteration array) is 49.774% of TestEntityQuery's 89.3s inclusive in that capture, i.e. ~44.5s = ~6.3% of ALL CPU in the profiled run. It is now a bigger target than CalcOwnerMask ever was (CalcOwnerMask was 2.1% of ALL CPU per the original VTune r006hs attribution that motivated bd_0ad-p8k).

WHAT: hoist an interface-presence bitmask into EntityData (source/simulation2/components/CCmpRangeManager.cpp), maintained alongside the existing ownerMask/flags fields added by bd_0ad-p8k and bd_0ad-ahy.1, so TestEntityQuery can do `entity.interfaceMask & (1ull << q.interface)` (a single load from a cache line already touched per-candidate) instead of chasing componentCache->interfaces[q.interface].

Design points to resolve:
- Check whether the interface-id space fits in 64 bits (bitmask feasibility). If it does not, consider an SoA side-array of u64 masks indexed parallel to the subdivision's entity list, to still eliminate the second pointer hop.
- Determine where componentCache/interfaces membership changes (component add/remove) and maintain the cached mask there, analogous to how ownerMask is maintained at the ownership-change site and recomputed on deserialize.
- Revisit static_assert(sizeof(EntityData) == 40) at CCmpRangeManager.cpp - adding a u64 (or reusing existing space) will change layout; same review pattern already paid down by bd_0ad-p8k/bd_0ad-ahy.1/bd_0ad-6uw.

Reference capture: C:\Users\james\0ad\captures\2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl (post bd_0ad-p8k fix). Also useful: pre-fix reference C:\Users\james\0ad\captures\2026-09-08_16-14-24_pyrogenesis.etl.
acceptance_criteria:
Debug and release builds compile. 
All tests are passing. 
A Superluminal profiling command is part of the final deliverable in order to validate performance impact.
notes:
Post-fix Superluminal capture reviewed (captures/2026-09-09_12-43-09_pyrogenesis.etl vs pre-fix baseline captures/2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl), by perf-guru.

CONFIRMED: the componentCache pointer-chase is eliminated from TestEntityQuery's hot path as designed. Source annotation shows zero attributed time on the componentCache fallback lines (only reachable for q.interface>=128, never hit in this workload); the replacement bit test `entity.interfaceMask[q.interface >> 6] & (1ull << (q.interface & 63))` sits at 15.03%, right alongside the existing `entity.ownerMask` test at 12.85% - the correct shape (same-cache-line bit test instead of a dependent load).

HEADLINE RESULT (defensible/normalized numbers): PerformQuery inclusive 199.83s -> 171.75s (-14.1% absolute, -7.6% per-call normalized: 71.59us -> 66.13us). This is below the originally predicted ~20% / 155-160s band - the prediction over-credited the fix by assuming the full ~44.4s pointer-chase cost would vanish, but part of that cost is actually the m_EntityData.find(id) cache-miss that fetches EntityData in the first place, which this fix does not touch (it only removes the second dependent hop after the fetch).

CAUTION - do not quote the raw -42.7% TestEntityQuery exclusive delta or the raw ForEachInRange<lambda_2> +8.4% delta: TestEntityQuery's TotalCallCount dropped 40.2% (1.485M -> 888,475) post-fix while PerformQuery/ForEachInRange call counts only moved ~7%. This is the signature of MSVC partially inlining the now-smaller TestEntityQuery into ForEachInRange's visitor at many call sites post-fix, not workload divergence - it moves cost between the two functions' attributed exclusive time without changing total work. The aggregate PerformQuery per-call number above is immune to this and is the trustworthy figure.

Follow-up for a clean, inlining-proof re-measurement if ever needed: rebuild with __declspec(noinline) on CCmpRangeManager::TestEntityQuery and recapture - pins call count at ~1.485M for a directly comparable per-function delta.
close_reason:
Implemented: added cached 128-bit interfaceMask (u64 interfaceMask[2]) to CCmpRangeManager::EntityData (source/simulation2/components/CCmpRangeManager.cpp), maintained alongside componentCache at both assignment sites (MT_Create ~line 651-652, RepopulateComponentCaches ~line 1048-1049 which also covers MT_Deserialized recompute). New static helper CalcInterfaceMask (~lines 109-116) derives the mask from the existing SEntityComponentCache. TestEntityQuery (~lines 1380-1394) now does a single bit test (entity.interfaceMask[q.interface >> 6] & (1ull << (q.interface & 63))) for IID < 128, falling back to the original componentCache pointer-chase only for IID >= 128 (kept for safety/future-proofing, not dead code). 128-bit width is required, not optional: code-explorer confirmed 49 native interfaces (TypeList.h) plus 64 public-mod script-registered interfaces (ComponentManager.cpp Script_RegisterInterface shares one ID counter with native registration) push real interface IDs to 113 — a 64-bit mask would silently break queries for any of the 50-113 range (which includes commonly-queried script interfaces). interfaceMask is derived, not serialized (same pattern as bd_0ad-p8k's ownerMask). static_assert(sizeof(EntityData)) updated 40 -> 56.

Verified (software-engineer + qa):
- Debug and Release builds compile clean, 0 warnings.
- 494/494 CxxTest tests pass (493 existing + 1 new regression test test_range_queries_required_interface_filtering added to test_RangeManager.h, which exercises the new bitmask fast-path directly with entities of differing component composition and confirms interface-filtered queries correctly include/exclude by interface presence).
- Code review confirmed all componentCache assignment sites are covered by the mask-maintenance call, control-flow/continue semantics preserved exactly, and no dynamic post-construction component-add path exists that could leave the mask stale (all AddComponent calls happen in ConstructEntity before CMessageCreate).

Superluminal validation command for the end user (elevated/admin shell required to run; consistent with bd_0ad-p8k/bd_0ad-ahy.1/bd_0ad-6uw/bd_0ad-v2l workload for direct comparison to pre-fix baseline captures/2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl):

What to check in the resulting capture (baseline: PerformQuery inclusive 199.83s, TestEntityQuery exclusive 89.29s, componentCache-chase line 49.774% of TestEntityQuery, ~44.4s): the componentCache-chase line should drop to near-zero in TestEntityQuery's source annotation (replaced by the mask-test line, expected in the same 5-12% band as the existing ownerMask test); TestEntityQuery exclusive should drop from 89.29s toward ~50-55s; PerformQuery inclusive should drop from 199.83s toward ~155-160s (~-20%). Also watch ForEachInRange<lambda_2> exclusive (baseline 89.59s) as a canary for the EntityData 40->56 byte layout growth possibly adding pressure to the m_EntityData.find(id) lookup — filed as follow-up bd_0ad-f6t regardless of outcome, not a blocker for this bead.

title: Spin-then-sleep TaskManager workers across back-to-back parallel sections
description: Follow-up from bd_0ad-92h. Consider a short spin-then-sleep in WorkerThread::RunUntilDeath (source/ps/TaskManager.cpp) so workers stay hot across back-to-back parallel sections instead of always parking on the condition_variable, reducing wake latency at the cost of some idle CPU burn. Deferred out of bd_0ad-92h scope; measure separately (tradeoff: cuts cross-section wake latency but can waste CPU on laptops / oversubscribed cores). Suggested approach: loop ~100-1000 iterations checking m_HasWork/m_HasLowPriorityWork/m_Kill with a pause/yield before falling back to condition_variable::wait, gated behind a tunable constant, default conservative (~200 iterations).
notes: Priority bumped P3->P1 per perf-guru review of captures/2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl: even after the 81c7cf96d6 wakeup-batching fix, TaskBatch::Flush->PushTasks->_Cnd_broadcast still costs 9.9s of main-thread executing time (5.7% of sim wall), plus 11.2s main-thread idle waiting on stragglers (Receiver::Wait). Workers average only ~38% useful-work efficiency inside their executing time. Wakeup/scheduling overhead is not solved, contrary to what closing bd_0ad-92h might have implied.

title: combat_demo_huge nonvisual speed=20 is non-deterministic run-to-run despite fixed seed
description:
WHY: discovered while validating bd_0ad-ahy.1's Superluminal before/after comparison. perf-guru found CCmpRangeManager::PerformQuery and TaskManager::PushTask call counts diverged between two captures of the same code at the same turn index (1,090,657 vs 1,066,013 PerformQuery calls at turn 19617, a -2.3% difference), which should be impossible for a deterministic fixed-seed AI-vs-AI sim.

QA investigated by running the UNMODIFIED (pre-ahy.1) build twice with identical args:
-autostart=\"scenarios/combat_demo_huge\" -autostart-nonvisual -autostart-player=-1 -autostart-speed=20 -autostart-victory=endless -autostart-disable-replay -autostart-seed=0 -autostart-aiseed=0

Result: 95.4% of turns (31,968 of 33,496 compared) had different PerformQuery call counts between the two runs of the IDENTICAL binary with the IDENTICAL seed. Typical per-turn variation was +/-15-30 calls, e.g. turn 1 had 1256 calls in run 1 vs 1214 in run 2 (-3.3%).

This confirms the nondeterminism is pre-existing and unrelated to bd_0ad-ahy.1 (that bead's flag-bit change was cleared of introducing it). It is presumably specific to -autostart-speed=20 nonvisual mode, since fixed-seed determinism is a core assumption of this engine's lockstep multiplayer/replay model.

IMPACT: this undermines the validity of any before/after profiling comparison on this workload that relies on matching call/query counts (only percentage-of-CPU normalized comparisons are trustworthy, per bd_0ad-ahy's own measurement-hazard notes) and is a correctness concern in its own right if it also affects OOS/replay/multiplayer determinism outside of profiling contexts.

WHAT: root-cause why combat_demo_huge at speed=20 nonvisual is non-deterministic across runs of the same binary/seed. Candidates to investigate: whether -autostart-speed=20's FastForward mechanism interacts with turn/timestep computation in a way that's sensitive to wall-clock/scheduling (e.g. variable-length real time slices being converted to a variable number of simulated turns or variable per-turn dt), whether AI decision timing depends on any real-time-derived value, or whether this is scoped only to nonvisual/observer fast-forward and does not affect normal-speed or player-driven determinism (which underpins replays and multiplayer sync).

Evidence: /scratchpad/FINAL_REPORT.md and counts_original_run1_trimmed.txt / counts_original_run2_trimmed.txt from the bd_0ad-ahy.1 QA investigation (paths under the QA subagent's temp scratchpad from 2026-09-08 — may need to be regenerated if not preserved).
notes: Priority bumped P2->P1 per perf-guru review: not itself a perf bug, but non-determinism invalidates every before/after performance measurement in the program (bd_0ad-1u1.2.4, bd_0ad-0pm, and verification of bd_0ad-117/xax/4yk all depend on comparable repeat captures). Treat as a blocking dependency for the perf workstream.
close_reason: Extensively investigated across multiple rounds; treated as non-reproducible on current entt-with-beads HEAD. Findings: (1) original bead hypothesis (wall-clock-driven CTurnManager::Update turn advancement) refuted -- -autostart-nonvisual advances turns via a fixed compile-time constant with no wall-clock read, and -autostart-speed=20 is a no-op in nonvisual mode. (2) A data-race hypothesis in CCmpRangeManager::ExecuteActiveQueries (raw pointers into m_Queries racing with DestroyActiveQuery) was investigated, a fix was even implemented, but an independent principal-engineer review traced the actual concurrency model and refuted it: the dispatching thread blocks synchronously in Future::Get() for the entire async window, so there is no reachable path for concurrent m_Queries mutation. The fix was reverted (would have added real allocation/perf regressions to fix a nonexistent bug). (3) A CCmpPathfinder/VertexPathfinder stale-scratch-buffer hypothesis was investigated and refuted on code inspection (dedicated per-thread instances, buffers cleared at end of each call). (4) Direct empirical verification via the canonical per-turn full-state-hash gate (-ooslog, the same mechanism used to validate bd_0ad-093.8/bd_0ad-bzj) was run twice against a freshly-verified-clean Release build (no debug hacks, confirmed via git status/diff and a devops-performed clean rebuild) with the exact original repro command (combat_demo_huge, -autostart-nonvisual -autostart-speed=20, fixed seed=0/aiseed=0, 3000 turns): all 3000 per-turn state hashes matched byte-for-byte across two independent runs. No divergence found. The original bug report's evidence was indirect (PerformQuery call-count deltas between two Superluminal profiler captures), which was not directly re-examined against current HEAD; it's possible that signal no longer reproduces due to intervening changes on this branch, or was itself a capture-overhead artifact rather than true state divergence. Reopen if profiling work resurfaces a discrepancy, ideally with a direct state-hash comparison alongside any call-count-based evidence.

    turn 5971, diverged at turn 5972; final lengths 6158 vs 5702 turns.
  - RangeManager reverted to the pre-8bb9f591a8 mutex-based version (same
    branch, same commit otherwise): runs matched through turn 1565, diverged
    at turn 1566; final lengths 1828 vs 1564 turns.
  CONCLUSION: the bug reproduces with and without 8bb9f591a8. That commit is
  not the cause (ruled out), though it does shift *where* divergence occurs,
  consistent with a timing-sensitive root cause rather than a logic bug in
  that function.

(2) Diffed main..entt-with-beads over source/ (43 commits, 27 files). Aside
from CCmpRangeManager.cpp (ruled out above) and the ahy.1 EntityData flag-bit
change (already cleared by QA per this issue's own description), every other
touched file is either: infra with no gameplay effect (Tracy thread naming/
zones, EnTT registry mirror bookkeeping in ComponentManager.cpp that nothing
in the live simulation reads yet -- no gameplay component has been ported off
the coexistence layer), or unrelated (Windows file-sharing mode for
concurrent processes, NetClient shutdown-ordering fix, -logDir/-autostart-
max-turns CLI args, GUI error dialog suppression, serializationtest optional
fix). None of these touch AI, pathfinding, RNG, or per-turn command handling.

LIKELY REAL MECHANISM (not yet confirmed by a main-branch build, see below):
CTurnManager::Update() advances simulated turns based on accumulated real
elapsed wall-clock time (m_DeltaSimTime += simFrameLength, capped at 2x turn
length backlog) -- see source/simulation2/system/TurnManager.cpp:73-160. This
is fundamentally wall-clock/scheduling sensitive, and -autostart-speed=20
nonvisual multiplies required throughput ~20x (per bd_0ad-o1z's own notes).
Any run-to-run variance in OS/thread scheduling or CPU throughput (including
totally incidental changes like a different RangeManager implementation)
would shift how many turns fit in a given real-time window and could change
which turn boundary an async AI decision's commands land on -- exactly
matching the observed pattern of "identical for N turns, then diverges, then
different total game length."

VERDICT: bd_0ad-ea4 is NOT a regression introduced by entt-with-beads. It is
almost certainly a pre-existing determinism hazard in the base engine's
real-time-gated turn pacing under nonvisual fast-forward, which would very
likely reproduce on main too (not yet empirically confirmed with a from-
scratch main build -- that would be the next step to close this out with
certainty). Safe to keep profiling this branch's changes using percentage-
normalized comparisons only, as already noted; no action needed on this
branch's commits to fix ea4 itself.

title: Hoist loop-invariant fixed-point terms out of CCmpUnitMotionManager::Push
description:
WHY: Superluminal (capture 2026-09-08_08-59-16) attributes 13.68s exclusive on the MAIN simulation thread to CCmpUnitMotionManager::Push (source/simulation2/components/CCmpUnitMotion_System.cpp:671), called per neighbouring unit pair per turn. Line-level annotation puts about half of that in fixed-point multiplies of terms that are constant for the whole turn:

  combinedClearance = maxDist.Multiply(movingPush ? m_MovingPushingSpread : m_StaticPushingSpread)  26.4 pct
  offset = ((a.pos + a.initialPos) - (b.pos + b.initialPos)) / 2                                    20.0 pct
  maxDist = combinedClearance.Multiply(m_PushingRadiusMultiplier) + (movingPush ? ... : ...)         13.7 pct
  combinedClearance = (a.cmpUnitMotion->m_Clearance + b.cmpUnitMotion->m_Clearance).Multiply(...)    10.8 pct

VTune r006hs corroborates the containing scope: CCmpUnitMotionManager::Move 5.84s.

m_PushingRadiusMultiplier, m_MovingPushingSpread, m_StaticPushingSpread, m_MovingPushExtension and m_StaticPushExtension are all constant for the turn. (a.second.pos + a.second.initialPos) is loop-invariant for the outer entity across all of its pair partners. The per-entity m_Clearance is also stable across the turn.

WHAT: precompute the two spread-scaled variants and the extension terms once per turn, and hoist the outer entity average position out of the inner pair loop.

DETERMINISM RISK - this is the main hazard. CFixed multiplication is not associative, so ALGEBRAIC rearrangement changes rounding and will diverge replays. Restructure by CACHING the exact same intermediate values only. Any change that alters the order or grouping of CFixed operations must be rejected even if it looks equivalent.
acceptance_criteria: Replay + state hash bit-identical - this is the primary gate, not the speedup. Measurable reduction in Push exclusive time at a fixed turn count. No change to pushing behaviour in formations or for idle units.
notes: Priority bumped P3->P1 per perf-guru review of captures/2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl: CCmpUnitMotionManager::Push is 27.1s = 15.5% of sim wall clock, fully serial (main thread). Three fixed::Multiply chains (lines with 11.5%/15.3%/27.6% of Push's cost = ~54%/14.8s) execute before the 8.9% CompareLength(maxDist) early-out that could skip them. Best wall-clock-per-effort bead currently open.

title: Race condition in CNetClient destructor: polling thread accesses m_ClientTurnManager during teardown
description: WHY: While validating bd_0ad-5z3's -autostart-max-turns feature in a two-process headless multiplayer scenario (host+client autostart with -serializationtest), both processes segfaulted (exit 139, access violation reading 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF) immediately after logging 'Reached max turns, quitting'. Root-caused via crash dump / instrumentation: CNetClient's polling thread remains active while the main thread destroys CNetClient in ~CNetClient() (source/network/NetClient.cpp), including members like m_ClientTurnManager that the polling thread concurrently accesses, causing memory corruption. This is a pre-existing latent race in CNetClient shutdown, not previously hit because normal network games end via other paths (window close, explicit disconnect UI flow) that apparently avoid this window, or because it is timing-sensitive and rare. The new -autostart-max-turns headless exit path (QuitEngine -> ShutdownNetworkAndUI -> EndGame -> SAFE_DELETE(g_NetClient)) hits it reliably. WHAT: fixed by reordering ~CNetClient() to call DestroyConnection() first (signals polling thread via m_ShouldShutdown) and clear m_GuiMessagePoll before proceeding with the rest of destruction, so the polling thread stops before shared state is torn down. Fix applied directly during bd_0ad-5z3 validation in source/network/NetClient.cpp (~13 lines). Filing this separately since it is a real, independently-scoped network-shutdown correctness bug (broader blast radius than serializationtest) even though it was fixed inline.
acceptance_criteria: Two-process headless multiplayer autostart with -autostart-max-turns reaches the turn limit and BOTH processes exit 0 cleanly with no segfault. Full CxxTest suite and x64 Debug+Release builds still pass with the destructor reordering in place. No new race/use-after-free introduced in normal (non-headless) multiplayer disconnect flows -- spot-check that a normal client disconnect/quit still works.
close_reason: Fixed serializationtest+autostart hang (Simulation2.cpp/Config.cpp/main.cpp: added -autostart-max-turns bound, fixed optional-type bug, added log observability); found and fixed two blocking issues surfaced during two-headless-client validation: Windows VFS deny-read sharing bug (wfilesystem.cpp ShareMode fix) and CNetClient destructor shutdown race (NetClient.cpp). x64 Debug+Release build clean, full CxxTest suite 493/493 passing, two-headless-client -serializationtest scenario runs to completion with clean exit 0 on both processes.

title: Cache entity Y in EntityData to kill per-candidate terrain resampling in parabolic range queries
description:
WHY: VTune r006hs (2026-09-03, scenarios/combat_demo_huge headless at speed 20, seeds pinned to 0) attributes 13.7 percent of ALL CPU (98s of 716.2s) to CCmpPosition::GetPosition called from the parabolic branch of CCmpRangeManager::PerformQuery (CCmpRangeManager.cpp:1399). For every candidate outside base range it constructs CmpPtr<ICmpPosition> (an interface hash lookup) and calls GetPosition(), which descends CCmpPosition::GetHeightAtFixed -> CCmpTerrain::GetGroundLevel -> CTerrain::GetExactGroundLevelFixed, burning 13.8s in CFixed::operator/ and 6.3s in Clamp on fixed-point terrain interpolation. The only value actually needed from that call is the target's Y.

WHAT: cache Y in EntityData alongside the x and z already stored there (CCmpRangeManager.cpp:263), maintained by the same position-change path that maintains x/z. That removes both the per-candidate ICmpPosition lookup and the terrain resampling in one change.

Design points to resolve:
- static_assert(sizeof(EntityData) == 24) at CCmpRangeManager.cpp:280 will need updating; check layout consequences, since EntityData is walked linearly via EntityMap in the hot loop.
- Determinism risk: cached Y must be invalidated on terrain deformation, not only on entity movement.

Not covered by bd_0ad-ahy, which scopes the interface-lookup cluster only and does not mention the terrain resampling at all.
acceptance_criteria: Parabolic queries no longer call ICmpPosition::GetPosition per candidate, and CTerrain::GetExactGroundLevelFixed no longer appears in the PerformQuery subtree. Query results bit-identical (replay + state hash). Before/after CPU time and instructions retired recorded at a fixed turn count.
notes:
=== INDEPENDENT CROSS-TOOL VALIDATION 2026-09-08 (Superluminal, ETW context-switch based) ===

Confirmed by a second profiler on the same code. Capture 2026-09-08_08-59-16_pyrogenesis. Normalised to the 664.4s real-work base (see the denominator warning on bd_0ad-ahy), the GetPosition subtree is 81.4s = 12.3 pct, against VTune 68.5s = 9.6 pct of total CPU. Close agreement from two different methodologies.

Chain confirmed by call graph, not inferred:
  PerformQuery -> CCmpPosition::GetPosition 81.4s incl
    -> CCmpPosition::GetHeightAtFixed 73.5s
    -> CCmpTerrain::GetGroundLevel 64.0s
    -> CTerrain::GetExactGroundLevelFixed 57.4s incl / 56.9s excl

USEFUL REFINEMENT - the cost is fixed-point ARITHMETIC, not heightmap memory access. Line annotation of Terrain.cpp:433-460:

  return ((one - zf).Multiply(xf1*h00 + xf0*h10) + zf.Multiply(xf1*h01 + xf0*h11)) / (HEIGHT_UNITS_PER_METRE/2)   51.276 pct
  xf = Clamp((x / TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE) - fixed::FromInt(xi), ...)                                                    9.826 pct
  zf = Clamp((z / TERRAIN_TILE_SIZE) - fixed::FromInt(zi), ...)                                                    6.217 pct
  the four m_Heightmap loads combined                                                                        about 3.2 pct

Consistent with the VTune split (CFixed::operator/ 14.5s, Clamp 6.5s). This means a heightmap layout or prefetch optimisation would buy almost nothing - only removing the CALL, as this issue proposes, captures the win.

BONUS SCOPE ALREADY IMPLIED: the parabolic call site carries a THIRD interface lookup per candidate on top of the two in TestEntityQuery. PerformQuery line costs:

  CmpPtr<ICmpPosition> cmpSecondPosition(GetSimContext(), subdivisionResultsBuffer[i])   6.839 pct
  !cmpSecondPosition || !cmpSecondPosition->IsInWorld()                                  8.386 pct
  CFixedVector3D secondPosition = cmpSecondPosition->GetPosition()                       15.726 pct

Caching Y removes all three, so this issue also cuts into the bd_0ad-ahy cluster, not just the terrain cost. Worth stating in the before/after.
=== POST-CHANGE SUPERLUMINAL VALIDATION 2026-09-08 (capture 2026-09-08_14-45-23_pyrogenesis) ===

Same workload/args as baseline: combat_demo_huge, -autostart-nonvisual -autostart-player=-1
-autostart-speed=20 -autostart-victory=endless -autostart-seed=0 -autostart-aiseed=0, --max-duration 180.
Baseline capture 2026-09-08_08-59-16 is no longer on disk; compared against the numbers
recorded in the note above.

DENOMINATOR NOTE (per bd_0ad-ahy warning): real-work CPU base rose 664.4s -> 769.3s at
constant 180s wall clock, i.e. the engine did ~16 pct MORE simulation work in the same
window. Absolute seconds are therefore NOT comparable; normalised shares and intra-function
line shares are used below.

RESULT: acceptance criteria met.

Process-wide (post), vs baseline PerformQuery-subtree figures:
  CCmpPosition::GetPosition           81.4s (12.3 pct)  -> 0.506s (0.066 pct)   -99.4 pct
  CCmpPosition::GetHeightAtFixed      73.5s             -> 0.480s
  CCmpTerrain::GetGroundLevel         64.0s             -> 0.359s
  CTerrain::GetExactGroundLevelFixed  57.4s (8.64 pct)  -> 0.292s (0.038 pct)   -99.5 pct

PerformQuery line annotation confirms the per-candidate cluster is gone. The three baseline
parabolic-branch lines totalling 30.95 pct of PerformQuery:
  CmpPtr cmpSecondPosition(...)                 6.839 pct  -> line no longer exists
  !cmpSecondPosition || !IsInWorld()            8.386 pct  -> line no longer exists
  secondPosition = cmpSecondPosition->GetPosition()  15.726 pct -> line no longer exists
replaced by:
  InParabolicRange(CFixedVector3D(it->second.x, it->second.y, it->second.z) - pos3d, range)
                                                            0.926 pct
So ~31 pct of PerformQuery's cost was eliminated, at constant per-call work.
Whole parabolic branch is now 34.6 pct of PerformQuery (post), of which GetNear 4.66 pct,
loop overhead 6.52 pct, TestEntityQuery 18.64 pct, EntityData::find 1.84 pct.

CRITERION 2 - PRECISE STATEMENT: GetExactGroundLevelFixed is no longer reachable PER
CANDIDATE, but it still appears under PerformQuery via the single per-query-source
GetPosition call. Measured on query worker Task Mgr #20 (ThreadKey 26):
  PerformQuery 34047.5ms incl
   -> CCmpPosition::GetPosition 44.2ms (0.13 pct of PerformQuery)
      -> GetHeightAtFixed 42.2ms -> CCmpTerrain::GetGroundLevel 30.2ms
That is exactly the one call per query the design intends (line at 0.195 pct of
PerformQuery == essentially the whole 0.506s process-wide GetPosition total, confirming
call count is per-query and not per-candidate). Removing it entirely is bd_0ad-1os.

CRITERION 4 CAVEAT: Superluminal is ETW context-switch/sampling based and does not expose
instructions retired. The instructions-retired confirmation that bd_0ad-ahy names as the
success metric would need a follow-up VTune run; only CPU time is measured here.

REMAINING HOTSPOT IN THE SAME FUNCTION (bd_0ad-ahy scope, untouched by this change):
CComponentManager::QueryInterface is still 10.25s of 34.05s = 30.1 pct of PerformQuery on
ThreadKey 26, from TestEntityQuery's two per-candidate interface lookups (the 18.639 pct
parabolic / 30.104 pct non-parabolic TestEntityQuery lines). This is now the single largest
cost inside PerformQuery.
close_reason: Implemented: cached entity Y in CCmpRangeManager::EntityData (new field after x/z, sizeof 24->28, not serialized) to eliminate the per-candidate CmpPtr<ICmpPosition>+GetPosition() lookup (and its bundled IsInWorld check) in PerformQuery's parabolic branch, removing CTerrain::GetExactGroundLevelFixed from that hot path entirely. Y kept in sync via MT_PositionChanged (in/out-of-world), MT_Deserialized (recompute all), and new MT_TerrainChanged/MT_WaterChanged subscriptions (recompute all, since deformation can change any entity's height without moving it); CCmpPosition's five height-only setters (SetHeightOffset/SetHeightFixed/SetHeightRelative/SetFloating/SetConstructionProgress) now push updates via new ICmpRangeManager::UpdateCachedHeight. Verified: Debug+Release build clean; 493/493 CxxTest pass both configs; -serializationtest clean (y correctly excluded from SerializeHelper); 600s+ headless combat_demo_huge run at speed=20 with fixed seed completed with no crash/assert/OOS. Code inspection confirms no per-candidate GetPosition/IsInWorld/GetExactGroundLevelFixed remains reachable from the parabolic branch. Superluminal before/after capture command recorded for pre-submit profiling step. Follow-up filed as bd_0ad-1os for remaining non-per-candidate GetPosition call sites in the same function.

title: Replace per-candidate ICmpMirage lookup in TestEntityQuery with an EntityData flag bit
description:
WHY: VTune r006hs (post-bd_0ad-o1z, 2026-09-03) shows CCmpRangeManager::TestEntityQuery performs two unconditional interface hash lookups per candidate entity per query (CCmpRangeManager.cpp:1367). One of them - CmpPtr<ICmpMirage> cmpMirage(GetSimContext(), id) - exists only to EXCLUDE mirage entities when q.preferMirages is false. It runs for every candidate of every query even when the world contains no mirage entities at all. Component lookup is 34.9 percent of engine CPU in that run (230.0s of 659.3s) and unordered_map::find alone is 142.8s, the largest single function in the profile.

WHAT: record mirage-ness as a bit in EntityData.flags instead of resolving the component. Bit 0x04 is already free and marked "// 0x04 reserved for future use" (CCmpRangeManager.cpp:246). EntityData is 24 bytes behind a static_assert (CCmpRangeManager.cpp:280) so a flag bit costs no size. Maintain it where the other flags are maintained (SetFlag calls around CCmpRangeManager.cpp:621-683) plus on mirage creation/destruction, then TestEntityQuery replaces the CmpPtr construction with entity.HasFlag<FlagMasks::Mirage>().

Unlike the general hoist proposed in the parent bd_0ad-ahy, this lookup is deletable rather than hoistable - no CEntityHandle/SEntityComponentCache plumbing required - so it is the cheapest available cut into the dominant bottleneck.
acceptance_criteria: TestEntityQuery performs no ICmpMirage interface lookup. Mirage filtering behaviour unchanged for both preferMirages=true and preferMirages=false. Determinism preserved (replay + state hash). Before/after instructions retired and CPU time recorded at a FIXED TURN COUNT, not a fixed wall-clock window - see the measurement hazard note on bd_0ad-ahy.
notes:
=== CROSS-TOOL CONFIRMATION 2026-09-08 (Superluminal) ===

Independently confirmed on the same code by an ETW-based profiler. TestEntityQuery is 17.251 pct (parabolic branch) and 20.904 pct (regular branch) of CCmpRangeManager::PerformQuery line cost - the single largest line in both branches. See bd_0ad-ahy for the denominator warning before comparing Superluminal shares to VTune shares.

SCOPE NOTE: the parabolic branch of PerformQuery does a THIRD interface lookup per candidate beyond the two this issue targets - CmpPtr<ICmpPosition> at 6.839 pct plus IsInWorld at 8.386 pct. That one is owned by bd_0ad-6uw (cache Y), which depends on this issue. Both edit EntityData and both must revisit static_assert(sizeof(EntityData) == 24) at CCmpRangeManager.cpp:280.

Consider sequencing this together with bd_0ad-p8k (precompute owner mask, 15.0s in the same function) so the EntityData layout review is paid once rather than three times.
close_reason: Implemented: mirage-ness moved from per-candidate CmpPtr<ICmpMirage> lookup to a precomputed EntityData flag bit (FlagMasks::Mirage=0x04), set once at entity creation. Verified: Debug+Release build clean; 493/493 CxxTest pass both configs; -serializationtest and 50-turn headless OOS run clean (0 errors/warnings); sizeof(EntityData) stays 24. Superluminal before/after capture (combat_demo_huge, same args, turn-matched window) confirms real improvement: QueryInterface calls per PerformQuery -13.7%, QueryInterface share of real-work CPU 26.07% -> 23.93% (-8.2% relative). A raw PerformQuery-count divergence between captures was investigated and confirmed to be pre-existing run-to-run nondeterminism in this workload at speed=20 nonvisual (reproduced on unmodified code, 95.4% of turns vary run-to-run with identical seed), not a correctness regression from this change.

title: Reduce lock and task granularity in CCmpRangeManager::ExecuteActiveQueries
description:
WHY: VTune profiling of a 1296-unit headless match shows the range-query work distribution is the single largest serialization point in the simulation, and it will swamp any measurement of the EnTT storage work (bd_0ad-1u1) if left in place.

Measured (Threading analysis r004tr, 180s, scenarios/combat_demo_huge, -autostart-nonvisual -autostart-player=-1 -autostart-speed=20, seeds pinned to 0):
- std::lock_guard<std::mutex>::{ctor}: 4,160,868 inactive sync waits (~23k/sec), 252.3s sync wait, 336.2s total inactive wait, 1,281,581 preemption waits.
- std::condition_variable::wait: 1,368,711 waits, 811.7s sync wait. 73.89 percent of all inactive wait time is workers idle on the pool condvar with no work.
- Effective CPU utilization 22.7 percent (5.44 of 24 logical CPUs).

Measured (uarch exploration r005ue, same command line):
- P-core Serializing Operations 25.1 percent of clockticks, Slow Pause 13.8 percent.
- Lock machinery ~306s CPU: RtlpAcquireSRWLockExclusiveContended 115.1s, RtlBackoff 81.0s (Slow Pause 64.4 percent = PAUSE spinning), KxWaitForLockOwnerShip 68.9s, RtlReleaseSRWLockExclusive 13.4s, ExpWaitForSpinLockSharedAndAcquire 11.7s, RtlAcquireSRWLockExclusive 9.7s, mtx_do_lock 6.7s. Plus RtlSleepConditionVariableSRW 99.0s.
- DRAM Bound 0.1 percent against 84 GB/s available, so this is serialization-bound, not bandwidth-bound.

Attribution confirmed by top-down call tree, not inferred: Threading::WorkerThread::RunUntilDeath -> PackagedTask<CCmpRangeManager::ExecuteActiveQueries> -> lambda_1::operator() -> lock_guard ctor. There is exactly one std::lock_guard in the whole simulation (grep over source/ excluding IO subsystems).

WHAT: source/simulation2/components/CCmpRangeManager.cpp:1181-1220. ExecuteActiveQueries farms queries to the worker pool, and each worker takes the shared mutex once per query purely to advance a std::map iterator and a message index:

    std::lock_guard lg(mtx);
    if (it == m_Queries.end()) break;
    itCopy = it++;
    idxCopy = messageIdx++;

Two separate problems, both from per-query granularity:
1. Mutex traffic. Batch N queries per acquisition, or replace the shared iterator with an atomic index over a pre-flattened vector of query pointers. Message ordering must stay fully deterministic (the existing comment at :1190-1192 is the constraint - messages are written to a fixed index to preserve order, so a flattened indexable container preserves that naturally).
2. Task size. 1.37M condvar round-trips means each task is far too small - workers wake, do one query, sleep. Batching queries per task addresses both at once.

CAVEAT on magnitudes: the uarch run inflates contention via observer effect (total CPU 1634s in r005ue vs 728s in the equivalent hotspots run r003hs, nearly all the delta in ntdll/ntoskrnl lock paths). The shape and existence of the contention are solid across three independent analysis types; treat the ~306s absolute as an upper bound. Also -autostart-speed=20 multiplies dispatch traffic ~20x versus normal play, so 4.16M acquisitions is not a 1x-play figure.
acceptance_criteria: Mutex acquisition count and condvar wait count in ExecuteActiveQueries reduced by at least an order of magnitude on the same pinned-seed combat_demo_huge run. Effective CPU utilization improved. P-core Serializing Operations share reduced. Determinism unchanged: range update message order identical, replay and state hash tests pass. Before/after VTune numbers recorded on this issue.
notes: VTune before/after validation (Release|x64, Arrowlake-S 24 logical CPU, combat_demo_huge -autostart-nonvisual -autostart-speed=20, hotspots hw sampling + stacks, --duration 180, identical command both runs). BEFORE = HEAD mutex version, AFTER = lock-free padded atomic batch cursor. Elapsed fixed at ~180.0s both runs by --duration, so throughput is measured as work completed in the fixed window, not wall time. THROUGHPUT: Instructions Retired 6,868,148,984,889 -> 7,486,602,169,322 (+9.0%); CPI Rate 0.504 -> 0.411 (-18.5%); Microarchitecture Usage 24.0% -> 27.8%; Total CPU Time 731.408s -> 712.408s. LOCK CONTENTION ELIMINATED: std::lock_guard<std::mutex>::{ctor} 92.396s (12.6% of all CPU, #2 hotspot overall) -> absent from top hotspots, 0.862s residual (-99.1%); Mtx_unlock 18.527s -> 0.076s (-99.6%); NtWaitForAlertByThreadId 54.403s -> 12.581s (-76.9%); RtlAcquireSRWLockExclusive 0.074s -> 0.006s; RtlReleaseSRWLockExclusive 0.066s -> 0.000s; RtlSleepConditionVariableSRW 0.029s -> 0.001s; aggregate lock+wait CPU ~177.9s -> ~25.9s (-152s, -85%). std::condition_variable::wait flat 10.992s -> 11.218s (task-manager idle, expected). REAL WORK SCALED UP in same wall clock, confirming worker threads now execute instead of blocking: CCmpRangeManager::PerformQuery 49.067s -> 60.147s (+22.6%); ExecuteActiveQueries worker lambda 4.719s -> 12.855s (+172%); EntityMap<EntityData>::find 12.800s -> 17.344s (+35.5%); CComponentManager::QueryInterface 65.203s -> 72.583s (+11.3%); _Hash<IComponent*>::find 120.640s -> 143.357s (+18.8%); CTerrain::GetExactGroundLevelFixed 16.655s -> 20.150s. Effective CPU Utilization 20.2% (4.839/24) -> 19.2% (4.613/24), a 1.0pp DIP that is NOT a regression: the MSVC mutex busy-spun in lock_guard::{ctor}/Mtx_unlock and VTune counted that spin as Effective Time, inflating the baseline; removing 152s of lock overhead lowers total CPU time while raising real work 9%. VERDICT: clear improvement, no regression. Spin Time flat (0.112s -> 0.110s). Repo left with fix restored and byte-identical (diffstat 62 ins / 52 del); nothing committed.

title: Fix measurement artifacts in EnTTStorageAccessBenchmark.cpp (accumulator floor, non-functional density axis, missing shuffled 1-pool baseline)
description:
WHY: perf-guru review of bd_0ad-1u1.1.6 found that the initial benchmark (source/tools/benchmarks/EnTTStorageAccessBenchmark.cpp) has methodology defects that invalidate parts of the (a)/(b)/(d) comparisons:
1. All benchmarks use a single serially-dependent scalar float accumulator (sum +=) under MSVC's default /fp:precise. This creates a ~4-cycle dependent-chain floor per loop iteration that masks the true cost of variant (a) virtual-accessor baseline and (b) registry::get<T>(e) -- both land at ~1.95-1.97ns/access, statistically indistinguishable, because both are pinned to the accumulator floor rather than reflecting their real relative cost. benchmark::DoNotOptimize(sum) outside the inner loop is insufficient to prevent this; the compiler can still hoist/restructure work inside the timed loop since the registry/entity vector are provably unmodified across outer iterations.
2. The BM_*_25Density variants iterate only over the subset vector of entities that actually carry the component (in creation order), which is arithmetically identical to a smaller 100%-density test -- it does not exercise sparse-index dilution/wasted cache-line fill at all. Confirmed by the results themselves showing no signal from the density axis.
3. There is no shuffled-order 1-pool baseline for the (d) multi-pool comparison, weakening the reported 3-pool-vs-1-pool ratio for shuffled access (only creation-order 1-pool exists).

WHAT: fix these three issues in the benchmark file:
- Use benchmark::DoNotOptimize() per-access (or an integer/bit-pattern accumulator via std::bit_cast) plus benchmark::ClobberMemory() before each inner timed loop, to force the compiler to actually perform and not reassociate/hoist each access.
- Rewrite the density variants to iterate ALL N entities and skip/read only the ~25% that carry the component (e.g. via pool->contains(e) or try_get), so the sparse-set index is genuinely touched sparsely.
- Add a BM_MultiPool_1Pool_ShuffledOrder benchmark to complete the (d) comparison matrix.
Re-run and update bd_0ad-1u1.1.6's recorded notes with corrected numbers once done; the current notes' (a)/(b) comparison and 25%-density conclusions should be flagged as superseded once this is fixed.
close_reason: Fixed accumulator-floor artifact, non-functional density axis, and missing shuffled-1-pool baseline in EnTTStorageAccessBenchmark.cpp. Verified by rebuild (Debug+Release x64 clean) and independent re-run; corrected numbers recorded on bd_0ad-1u1.1.6.

title: Re-measure EnTT 1/2/3-pool storage split with CCmpPosition-sized structs and N sweep
description:
WHY: perf-guru review of bd_0ad-1u1.1.6's benchmark (source/tools/benchmarks/EnTTStorageAccessBenchmark.cpp) found the storage structs used (8-12 bytes) are an order of magnitude smaller than a real ported component like CCmpPosition (~110-120 bytes). This biases the multi-pool-split measurement favorably: small structs let 3 pools' combined working set stay L2-resident and get cache-line amortization that a real component won't get, understating the true multi-pool penalty that ADR-001 Appendix A's Template/State/Derived split will incur. Additionally only N=10k was tested, giving no visibility into an L2-cliff at larger entity counts.

WHAT: extend or add a benchmark variant using CCmpPosition-shaped POD structs (~110-120 bytes total, split plausibly across Template/State/Derived) for the 1/2/3-pool comparison, and sweep N across at least 1k/10k/100k entities to see whether/where a cache-capacity cliff appears. This should be the measurement that actually gates whether ADR-001 Appendix A's 3-way split needs amending, superseding the current (undersized-struct) 3-pool numbers recorded on bd_0ad-1u1.1.6.
