- VTune r006hs: 3.99s CPU at CPI 1.372, versus about 0.41 for essentially every other hot function - 3.3x worse. It retires only 8.47 billion instructions for that time, i.e. almost pure pointer-chase stall, unlike the interface-lookup cluster in bd_0ad-ahy which is instruction-bound at high IPC.
- Superluminal (capture 2026-09-08_08-59-16): 5.17s exclusive inside map::operator[], under SetUnitMovingFlag (5.60s) under CCmpUnitMotionManager::Move (33.0s) on the main thread.

Because this sits on the critical path rather than the worker pool, its wall-clock value is higher than its CPU share suggests.

WHAT: tags are dense small indices (TAG_TO_INDEX), so replace the red-black tree with vector-backed slot storage.

Check the other m_UnitShapes uses before choosing a representation:
- linear iteration at line 284
- insertion at line 303 (m_UnitShapes[id] = shape)
- serialization at line 213 (Serializer over the map)
The serialization path is the binding constraint - it must keep producing byte-identical output, or the change breaks determinism and save/load compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: SetUnitMovingFlag performs no tree lookup. Serialized simulation state byte-identical. Replay + state hash unchanged. CPI for the flag-set path recorded before/after.
notes: Priority bumped P3->P2 per perf-guru review: std::map<UnitShape>::operator[] in SetUnitMovingFlag path costs 8.08s exclusive, 100% on main thread = 4.6% of sim wall clock. Trivially fixable, good ROI.

title: Hoist subdivision buffer size out of the PerformQuery candidate loops
description:
WHY: the parent bd_0ad-v2l reads the VTune vector::size entries (34.6s + 8.9s) as inlined-frame wrappers around FastSpatialSubdivision::GetInRange. Superluminal line-level annotation of PerformQuery (capture 2026-09-08_08-59-16) shows that is only partly right - the GetNear call line and the for-loop CONDITION line carry separate and roughly EQUAL cost, in both branches of CCmpRangeManager::PerformQuery:

  parabolic branch:
    m_Subdivision.GetNear(subdivisionResultsBuffer, pos, subdivisionRange)   3.178 pct of PerformQuery
    for (size_t i = 0; i < subdivisionResultsBuffer.size(); ++i)             3.184 pct
  regular branch:
    m_Subdivision.GetNear(subdivisionResultsBuffer, pos, q.maxRange)         8.155 pct
    for (size_t i = 0; i < subdivisionResultsBuffer.size(); ++i)             8.343 pct

So roughly half of the vector::size cost attributed to this cluster is the loop bound reload, not the gather. Consistent with the VTune addresses: the two entries sit at 0x140111180 and 0x140110e0c, both inside PerformQuery (start 0x140110ac0), i.e. the two candidate loops. The compiler cannot hoist the load because r.push_back(it->first) into the result vector may alias subdivisionResultsBuffer.

Combined that is 44.6s of 716.2s = 6.2 percent of ALL CPU in r006hs.

WHAT: hoist the bound to a local before each loop:

  const size_t candidateCount = subdivisionResultsBuffer.size();
  for (size_t i = 0; i < candidateCount; ++i)

Neither loop body modifies subdivisionResultsBuffer, so this is behaviour-preserving. Independent of the parent issue - it can land first, is near-zero risk, and does not require deciding on the larger gather redesign.
acceptance_criteria: Both PerformQuery candidate loops read the buffer size once. Instructions retired down measurably in the PerformQuery subtree. Query results bit-identical (replay + state hash). Measured at a fixed turn count, not a fixed wall-clock window.
notes: Obsoleted by the bd_0ad-v2l implementation. The for (size_t i = 0; i < subdivisionResultsBuffer.size(); ++i) loops this bead targeted no longer exist - PerformQuery's candidate loops were rewritten to use ForEachNear + a visitor lambda, with subdivisionResultsBuffer and the per-worker buffer plumbing removed entirely. No loop-bound-reload cost remains to hoist.

title: Fan out TaskManager wakeups without waking every worker per task
description:
WHY: Threading::TaskManager::Impl::PushTask (source/ps/TaskManager.cpp:194-207) notifies EVERY worker for EVERY task pushed:

    for (WorkerThread& worker : m_Workers)
        worker.Wake();

Each WorkerThread owns a private std::mutex + std::condition_variable, so this is one notify_one per worker per task - O(W^2) kernel transitions per parallel section. CCmpRangeManager::ExecuteActiveQueries pushes numFutures = min(GetNumberOfWorkers(), n) = 23 tasks per turn on this machine, so about 529 wakeups per turn. Woken workers evaluate the predicate, contend on m_GlobalMutex in PopTask, mostly find nothing, and sleep again (thundering herd).

MEASUREMENT - the two profilers disagree sharply on this path and NEITHER is trustworthy here. Scope expectations accordingly:

- Superluminal (ETW context-switch based, capture 2026-09-08_08-59-16) puts 115.1s of the 170.0s main-thread Running-state window inside _Cnd_signal -> ZwAlertThreadByThreadId, plus 238.7s of pool Running-state inside _Cnd_wait. That is 354s of 1018s total Running-state.
- VTune r006hs (EBS/PMU, same code) sees essentially none of it. No _Cnd_signal or ZwAlertThreadByThreadId sample at all. ZwWaitForAlertByThreadId 11.98s, std::condition_variable::wait 11.24s, RtlSleepConditionVariableSRW 0.04s. Whole-process ntdll is 12.4s and ntoskrnl 25.7s across all 35 threads.

RECONCILIATION: the main thread genuinely sits in the wake path for most of its wall time, but that is scheduler and IPI latency rather than retired cycles. Corroborating displaced cost: KiDpcInterruptBypass 23.2s + KiExecuteAllDpcs 1.3s of ntoskrnl CPU, consistent with cross-core wakeup IPI traffic. VTune also contradicts itself in this region - it reports ZwWaitForAlertByThreadId at 2.24 trillion instructions retired against 11.98s CPU, i.e. 187 G instr/sec on a 3.07 GHz part, which is impossible and marks the region as an attribution artifact.

Expected win is critical-path LATENCY plus roughly 25-40s of kernel/DPC CPU - NOT the 115s a naive read of the Superluminal capture suggests.

WHAT:
- Replace the per-worker mutex/condvar with a single pool-wide mutex + condition_variable, notify_one per task pushed.
- Add a batch push API (a span of tasks) so ExecuteActiveQueries enqueues all N tasks under one lock and issues a single notify_all.
- Consider a short spin-then-sleep in WorkerThread::RunUntilDeath so workers stay hot across back-to-back parallel sections.
acceptance_criteria: Wall-clock turn time improves at a FIXED TURN COUNT - do not accept on profiler CPU attribution for this path, see the measurement hazard note on bd_0ad-ahy and the tool-divergence note on this issue. Determinism preserved (replay + state hash). No change to task execution order guarantees.
notes:
FALSE SIGNAL TO IGNORE - apparent worker load imbalance.

Superluminal per-thread CaptureCpuUtilization on the 23 Task Mgr threads shows a 5.31x spread (79.6s down to 15.0s executing; 44 percent down to 8 percent utilization), which reads like severe load imbalance in the ExecuteActiveQueries fan-out. It is NOT.

VTune r006hs per-thread CPU on the same code shows only a 1.56x spread:
  main 86.35s | 37.35 32.81 32.64 32.13 31.65 31.34 30.76 26.74 26.48 26.42
              | 25.89 25.50 25.46 24.94 24.91 24.78 24.64 24.52 24.47 24.25
              | 24.18 24.09 23.90
with 18 of 23 workers clustered in 23.9-26.7s. The atomic batch cursor from bd_0ad-o1z distributes query work correctly.

The Superluminal curve is measuring WAKE ORDER, not work: workers early in m_Workers get notify_one first, enter Running state, fail to find work, and sleep again, accruing Running-state time each round. That is further evidence for the thundering herd this issue fixes, but it is not evidence of unequal useful work - do not add work-stealing or partitioning on the strength of it.
close_reason: Implemented pool-wide mutex/condvar + PushTasks/TaskBatch batching per blueprint; CCmpRangeManager::ExecuteActiveQueries now batches its per-turn Future pushes. Debug+Release build clean, full CxxTest suite (493 tests) passing in both configs, qa confirmed meaningful concurrency test coverage (test_Load: 100k futures/3 threads) and no ordering/determinism regression. Follow-up spin-then-sleep idea filed as bd_0ad-jto.

title: Windows loose-file VFS opens use deny-read sharing, breaking concurrent multi-process pyrogenesis
description: WHY: While validating bd_0ad-5z3 (serializationtest+autostart fix) with a two-headless-client scenario, found that -serializationtest's per-turn secondary-simulation rebuild (which reloads ~250 globalscripts/*.js files per turn) crashes almost immediately when TWO pyrogenesis processes run concurrently on the same machine, with 'CVFSFile: file globalscripts/AttackEffects.js couldn't be opened (vfs_load: -110300)' cascading into a fatal JS error (ModificationsSchema is not defined) and process abort. WHAT: source/lib/sysdep/os/win/wposix/wfilesystem.cpp wopen() (both the 2-arg and 3-arg overloads, lines ~36-63) hardcodes _SH_DENYRD for the blocking (non-O_DIRECT/non-aio) file-open path, meaning any read-only open denies OTHER PROCESSES read access for the handle's lifetime. This differs from the aio path (waio.cpp ShareMode(), line ~76-90) which correctly returns FILE_SHARE_READ for O_RDONLY. Two processes opening the same loose file (or the same mounted .zip archive, which is worse since archive_zip.cpp holds an open handle for the whole process lifetime) will hit ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION -> EACCES -> ERR::FILE_ACCESS (-110300). Root-caused by principal-engineer during bd_0ad-5z3 validation; confirmed NOT a regression from that fix (diff there only touches Simulation2.cpp/Config.cpp/main.cpp, no VFS/file-loading code) - it is a pre-existing bug that bd_0ad-5z3 merely made reachable (by turning an unbounded hang into a run that reaches the point where two processes' load storms overlap). Blast radius is broader than serializationtest: any two concurrent pyrogenesis processes on Windows (headless MP, replay-alongside-game, test.exe alongside game, atlas+game) can hit this, worse on archived/release installs.
acceptance_criteria: Fix wopen() in source/lib/sysdep/os/win/wposix/wfilesystem.cpp to derive share mode from oflag (mirror waio.cpp ShareMode()): O_RDONLY -> _SH_DENYWR (allow other readers), O_WRONLY/O_RDWR -> keep _SH_DENYRD or _SH_DENYRW. Two headless client processes (host+client) running -autostart-host/-autostart-client with -serializationtest=<turn> -autostart-max-turns=<N> against the same scenario map must both run to completion (max turns reached) and exit 0, with no vfs_load/File_OpenFailed errors in either log. Full x64 Debug+Release builds and full CxxTest suite (test.exe, all tests) must still pass.
close_reason: Fixed serializationtest+autostart hang (Simulation2.cpp/Config.cpp/main.cpp: added -autostart-max-turns bound, fixed optional-type bug, added log observability); found and fixed two blocking issues surfaced during two-headless-client validation: Windows VFS deny-read sharing bug (wfilesystem.cpp ShareMode fix) and CNetClient destructor shutdown race (NetClient.cpp). x64 Debug+Release build clean, full CxxTest suite 493/493 passing, two-headless-client -serializationtest scenario runs to completion with clean exit 0 on both processes.

title: Reduce result-buffer copying in FastSpatialSubdivision::GetInRange candidate gather
description:
WHY: VTune r006hs (2026-09-03) attributes ~14.7 percent of total CPU (~105s of 716.2s) to the spatial subdivision candidate gather inside CCmpRangeManager::PerformQuery. Symbols are smeared across inlined frames - the parent shows as std::vector<unsigned int>::size with 34.6s and 8.9s self at the two call sites, wrapping FastSpatialSubdivision::GetInRange - but the ancestry is confirmed by top-down, not inferred:

  PerformQuery -> [vector::size inline frame] -> FastSpatialSubdivision::GetInRange
    -> vector::_Insert_counted_range (21.3s + 6.8s self) -> memcpy (8.4s + 5.0s self)

So roughly 40s of the ~105s is pure copying of per-tile entity ID lists into the result buffer.

This is also the genuine memory-stall site in the profile, in contrast to the interface-lookup cluster: bd_0ad-ahy records these buffers at CPI 1.07-1.21 with Memory Bound 56.6-66.6 percent. So unlike bd_0ad-ahy, instruction count is not the only lever here - locality changes should show a real win.

WHAT: investigate avoiding the append-and-copy. Options to evaluate:
- iterate tile buckets directly and test candidates in place rather than materialising a combined vector;
- reserve the result buffer to a high-water mark to eliminate reallocation;
- store subdivision buckets so a range scan is contiguous.
Note m_SubdivisionResultBuffers is already a per-worker buffer reused across queries (see the ExecuteActiveQueries fan-out from bd_0ad-o1z), so the remaining cost is the copy itself, not allocation churn.
acceptance_criteria: Measurable reduction in the GetInRange subtree share of the PerformQuery subtree. Query results bit-identical (replay + state hash). Before/after CPU time and instructions retired recorded at a fixed turn count.
notes:
=== SUPERLUMINAL 2026-09-08: interpretation correction + refinement ===

CORRECTION to this description. It reads the VTune vector::size entries (34.6s + 8.9s) as inlined-frame wrappers around FastSpatialSubdivision::GetInRange. Superluminal line-level data shows that is only partly right: roughly HALF of that cost is the PerformQuery for-loop CONDITION reloading subdivisionResultsBuffer.size() each iteration, which is a separate and much cheaper fix. Split out as child bd_0ad-v2l.1 - it can land first, independently of the gather redesign.

REFINEMENT on the copy itself, which this issue still owns. Superluminal: GetInRange 60.0s inclusive / 14.4s exclusive, with vector::_Insert_counted_range 45.7s inclusive / 31.6s exclusive beneath it. Line annotation of Spatial.h:531-559:

  out.insert(out.end(), subdivision.begin(), subdivision.end())   88.693 pct of GetInRange
  if (!subdivision.empty())                                        5.375 pct
  m_SpatialDivisionsData[X + Y*m_ArrayWidth]                       2.414 pct
  out.insert(... m_OverSizedData ...)                              0.689 pct

Within GetInRange the bucket copy is essentially the ENTIRE cost. That is a steer between the three options listed in the description: reserving to a high-water mark removes reallocation but NOT the copy, so it will underdeliver. Prefer iterating tile buckets directly and testing candidates in place (a visitor overload taking a callable), which removes the copy outright.

Note the buffers are already per-worker and reused across queries, so allocation churn is already largely amortised - reinforcing that reserve alone is the weak option.
RESOLVED. Implemented the visitor/callback redesign (ForEachInRange/ForEachNear template methods in Spatial.h) replacing the materialize-into-vector pattern, per the principal-engineer design that also subsumed bd_0ad-9oj. CCmpRangeManager::PerformQuery's two candidate loops now use ForEachNear + lambda visitor; removed now-unused m_SubdivisionResultBuffers plumbing entirely.

VALIDATION:
- Debug + Release builds clean (devops).
- All 493 CxxTest tests pass; determinism re-verified via repeated combat_demo autostart replay producing byte-identical mainlog.html (qa).
- Post-fix Superluminal capture (2026-09-08_16-14-24_pyrogenesis, combat_demo_huge workload) confirms the acceptance criterion decisively (perf-guru):
  - Old vector<uint32_t>::_Insert_counted_range (baseline: 45.7s inclusive/31.6s exclusive under GetInRange, 76pct of GetInRange's 60.0s inclusive) is GONE - zero occurrences in the new capture. GetInRange/GetNear symbols themselves are gone from the hot path (both fully inlined into ForEachInRange, which is itself inlined for GetNear).
  - ForEachInRange (both branch instantiations) = 108.4s inclusive / 50.7s exclusive = 98.1pct/45.9pct of PerformQuery's 110.5s inclusive. Of that exclusive time, ~86-90pct is now the visitor(id) line itself (real per-candidate work: find + TestEntityQuery + distance math), with only ~9.5-14pct being bucket-loop traversal overhead (pointer chasing, not copying).
  - Bottleneck has cleanly shifted to TestEntityQuery (57.5s exclusive = 52.1pct of PerformQuery, #2 function in the whole capture) - already tracked as bd_0ad-p8k, bumped to P2 given this new share.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED:
- bd_0ad-p8k bumped P3->P2 (owner-mask precompute, now the dominant remaining cost).
- bd_0ad-783 (new, P3): parabolic branch over-scans ~4x area via flat 2x radius inflation; candidates gathered but rejected at a higher rate than the regular branch.

Per acceptance criteria: query results bit-identical (replay+state-hash via qa), measurable reduction in GetInRange subtree share of PerformQuery (copy cost 0ms vs 45.7s baseline), before/after CPU recorded via Superluminal at combat_demo_huge fixed workload.

title: -serializationtest hangs/loops forever when combined with -autostart (unsupported combo, config-based code path)
description: WHY: While validating determinism for bd_0ad-o1z (RangeManager lock removal), discovered that passing -serializationtest=<turn> together with -autostart=<map> -autostart-nonvisual causes pyrogenesis.exe to loop forever re-running CSimulation2Impl construction (repeatedly logging all ~213 'Loading simulation script' lines in an apparent tight loop, never progressing to actual simulation turns or exiting). Confirmed via 60s timeout tests on a tiny map (scenarios/arcadia, no speed multiplier): ~27-28k duplicate 'Loading simulation script' log lines in 60s and climbing, process never exits. CONFIRMED PRE-EXISTING AND UNRELATED TO bd_0ad-o1z: reproduced identically on the pre-fix CCmpRangeManager.cpp (git stash test on commit e177e7eb07, before the ExecuteActiveQueries lock-removal change) with the same command - 26971 vs 27720 lines in 60s, same infinite-timeout behavior on both. WHAT: source/main.cpp:610-637 only wires -serializationtest through CReplayPlayer::Replay() in the isNonVisualReplay branch (i.e. when -replay=<path> is passed). When -autostart is used instead of -replay, -serializationtest is picked up by a DIFFERENT, apparently-broken path: ps/GameSetup/Config.cpp:91-94 stores it in CConfigDB, and simulation2/Simulation2.cpp:88-93 reads it back as m_SerializationTestTurn via CConfigDB::GetIfInitialised. Something in that config-driven path causes the simulation/component-manager construction to repeat indefinitely instead of running normally to the target turn. This combination (-autostart + -serializationtest, without -replay) is not the documented usage (source/simulation2/docs/EnTT-Determinism-Rules.md point 7 explicitly recommends 'pyrogenesis -replay=<path> -serializationtest=<divergent turn>'), so it may be a dead/untested code path, but it is still a real bug (infinite loop is a much worse failure mode than an error message) and should either be fixed or explicitly rejected with a clear error at startup if -serializationtest is given without -replay.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) -autostart-seed=0 -autostart=<map> -serializationtest=<turn> completes normally (progresses to the target turn, runs the serialization round-trip check, and exits/continues) without looping, or (b) pyrogenesis.exe rejects the -serializationtest flag with a clear startup error/warning when -replay is not also specified, instead of hanging.
close_reason: Fixed -serializationtest+-autostart: root cause was not an infinite loop but a per-turn full secondary-simulation rebuild (~2 turns/sec) with no bounded exit; fixed a latent std::optional bug in Simulation2.cpp, added log observability, and added -autostart-max-turns to bound headless runs (Simulation2.cpp/Config.cpp/main.cpp). Two additional pre-existing bugs were found and fixed while validating the two-headless-client acceptance criterion: Windows VFS deny-read sharing violation (bd_0ad-dph, wfilesystem.cpp) and a CNetClient destructor shutdown race (bd_0ad-fpd, NetClient.cpp). Verified: x64 Debug+Release build clean; full CxxTest suite 493/493 passing (confirmed the one transient failure was pre-existing/flaky via baseline comparison); two-headless-client -serializationtest run completes to the turn bound with clean exit 0 on both host and client, no OOS/VFS/crash errors; normal multiplayer disconnect path regression-checked with no new issues from the NetClient fix.

title: Investigate simulation worker thread placement on E-cores (hybrid CPU scheduling)
description:
WHY: on a hybrid Intel part the simulation worker pool is landing predominantly on efficiency cores, which costs throughput and makes the atomics in the range-query dispatch loop more expensive. Worth knowing whether this is worth influencing before optimizing around it.

Measured (VTune uarch exploration r005ue, 180s, scenarios/combat_demo_huge headless at 20x, Core Ultra 9 275HX / Arrowlake-S, 24 logical CPUs):
- Clockticks: 4.985 T on E-cores vs 2.349 T on P-cores (68 percent E-core).
- Instructions retired: 7.529 T on E-cores vs 4.795 T on P-cores (61 percent E-core).
- CPI: E-core 0.662 vs P-core 0.490.
- E-core Core Bound 31.8 percent of pipeline slots, of which Serializing Operations 21.9 percent and Fence 17.9 percent - the dispatch-loop atomics are notably more expensive on E-cores.
- Threading analysis r004tr recorded 703,488 preemption waits, consistent with heavy cross-core migration.

WHAT: determine whether 0ad should express any thread-priority or affinity preference for simulation worker threads (source/ps/ThreadUtil, Threading::WorkerThread / TaskManager), or whether this is purely an OS scheduler concern to be left alone. Options to evaluate: leave as-is (document the finding), raise worker thread priority so the Windows scheduler prefers P-cores, or set explicit affinity. Affinity is likely the wrong answer - it is fragile across CPU topologies and would need per-platform detection - so the realistic outcome may be "document and do not act".

Depends on bd_0ad-o1z: if the dispatch loop is fixed to use coarse batched tasks, the per-task atomic and preemption traffic drops and this may stop mattering. Re-measure after that lands before investing here.

CAVEAT: single-machine, single-CPU-model observation. Do not generalize to other hybrid parts or to non-hybrid CPUs without re-measuring. -autostart-speed=20 also inflates task-dispatch traffic ~20x versus normal play.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision, with numbers, on whether to influence worker thread placement. If no action: the finding is documented (ADR or issue notes) with the measured P/E split so it is not rediscovered. If action: before/after P/E clocktick split and CPI on the same pinned-seed run.
notes: Priority bumped P3->P2 per perf-guru review: workers burn ~15s of 24.8s executing time (over the capture) on non-query overhead; effective parallel speedup on the query phase is only ~4x from 30 threads. Scheduling/core-placement is a first-order problem, not just a curiosity, per captures/2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl.

title: Add CLI arg to redirect the directory where replays are stored
Windows build: benchmark lib not wired into libraries/win64 (same bootstrap-reproducibility gap as entt)
description: WHY: discovered by principal-engineer while designing the fix for bd_0ad-5je (entt header-only include path bug). The 'benchmark' extern lib entry in build/premake/extern_libs5.lua uses add_source_include_paths/add_source_lib_paths, which on Windows resolve into libraries/win64/benchmark/. But libraries/win64/ is the SVN-managed prebuilt bundle fetched by get-windows-libs.bat, and (unlike fcollada/nvtt/spidermonkey) there is no benchmark directory in that bundle -- Google Benchmark is vendored as source (libraries/source/benchmark) like entt. Unlike entt, benchmark is a REAL compiled library (not header-only), so the fix is different from bd_0ad-5je's header-only-include-path fix: it likely needs an actual Windows build step/script that compiles libraries/source/benchmark and stages the .lib/.h output into libraries/win64/benchmark/, or an equivalent premake-side special case. NOT YET CONFIRMED whether a clean Windows checkout can currently build the 'benchmarks' target; needs verification (attempt premake + msbuild of the benchmarks project on a checkout without a hand-populated libraries/win64/benchmark/) before deciding the exact fix.
acceptance_criteria: Clean Windows checkout (get-windows-libs.bat + build-source-libs + premake + msbuild) can build the 'benchmarks' target with no manual file staging, OR this bead is closed as not-a-bug if investigation shows benchmark is already correctly bootstrapped on Windows via some other existing mechanism.
close_reason: Fixed benchmark lib Windows wiring: added add_source_only_include_paths/add_source_only_lib_paths helpers in extern_libs5.lua pointing at libraries/source/benchmark on all platforms (same bug class as EnTT fix bd_0ad-5je, but for a compiled lib); ran build.sh to produce benchmark.lib/benchmarkd.lib; regenerated VS2022 solution. Verified Debug|x64 and Release|x64 build cleanly (benchmarks/pyrogenesis/test, no regressions) and all 493 CxxTest tests pass in both configs.

title: Convert one hot CCmpPosition consumer to direct pool iteration (net-perf validation for the EnTT milestone)
description:
WHY: as designed, the coexistence layer makes per-access cost WORSE, not better. Even with EnTTComponent's cached pool pointers, Get<T>() is ~5-6 serially dependent loads over 3-4 cache lines (both the sparse index at ENTT_SPARSE_PAGE=4096 and the payload at ENTT_PACKED_PAGE=1024 are paged) versus 1 usually-hot load for the member variable it replaces. Because each access already sits behind a virtual ICmpX call, the marginal cost is more like +30-60% per accessor call than 6x - but it is an increase. The payoff only arrives when a real system iterates a pool directly and the sparse lookup disappears entirely.

Consequence: porting CCmpPosition (bd_0ad-1u1.2.2) on its own lands a measurable regression with no offsetting win, and the milestone would have to be judged on faith rather than on numbers.

WHAT: after CCmpPosition is registry-backed, convert one genuinely hot consumer to direct pool iteration so the milestone can be evaluated on NET performance. Interpolation is the obvious candidate: it touches every entity every frame and is per-entity order-independent, so it is permitted under ADR-001 Decision 4 (per-entity pure updates writing only components of the same entity). Must ship with an explicit determinism argument at the loop per Decision 4, and must not introduce order-sensitive mutation, shared-state accumulation, RNG consumption, message emission, or entity creation/destruction in view-iteration order.

Note ADR-001 Decision 5: multi-component views spanning several migrated types are an explicitly scoped later optimisation, so keep this to a single-pool iteration unless the scope is widened deliberately.
acceptance_criteria: One hot CCmpPosition consumer iterates its storage pool directly instead of going through per-entity proxy accessors, with a determinism argument documented at the loop. Before/after numbers recorded showing the net effect of the CCmpPosition migration.
notes: Kept at P2 per perf-guru review, but scope note: this is the only bead in the EnTT epic that can produce real perf evidence. Consider pointing it at the motion-manager iteration path (48% of sim wall clock per captures/2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl) rather than a Position accessor, since CCmpPosition itself is only 0.2% of CPU.

title: Guard the ResetState invariant: all proxies destroyed before the entt::registry object is replaced
description:
WHY: EnTTComponent<> (bd_0ad-1u1.1.3) caches an entt::registry* plus one storage-pool pointer per storage struct in each component proxy. Pool addresses are stable for the registry's lifetime (pools holds std::allocate_shared'd storage objects, so rehashing pools moves shared_ptrs, not the pooled objects), but they are NOT stable across replacement of the registry object itself. registry::swap() and operator=(basic_registry&&) (implemented as swap, registry.hpp:343) both invalidate every cached pool pointer, as does registry::reset(id) (registry.hpp:435), which erases a pool outright.

CComponentManager::ResetState() already satisfies the required invariant - the Deinit() + dealloc() loop runs before 'm_Registry = std::make_unique<entt::registry>()' - but this is currently only implied by statement ordering. Any future reordering silently produces proxies holding dangling pool pointers, which is a use-after-free with no diagnostic.

WHAT: add an ENSURE (or equivalent) in ResetState() asserting that no component proxies remain live at the point the registry is replaced (e.g. m_ComponentsByTypeId empty / a live-proxy counter at zero). Also consider a debug-only guard against registry::reset() ever being called. Deliberately NOT done in bd_0ad-1u1.1.3, whose acceptance criterion forbids CComponentManager call-site changes beyond the lifecycle hooks landed in bd_0ad-1u1.1.2. The invariant is documented in ADR-001 Appendix A.
acceptance_criteria: ResetState() fails loudly in a debug build if any component proxy is still live when the registry object is replaced. Existing test suite stays green.
close_reason: Added ENSURE(m_ComponentsByTypeId.empty()) in ResetState() before registry replacement, plus invariant documentation on GetRegistry(). QA verified placement/no-false-positives/486 tests pass (Debug+Release). Perf-guru verified negligible cost in cold path (ResetState only runs on sim reset/load, not per-turn/per-frame).

title: Port CCmpPosition to EnTT-backed storage behind the coexistence layer
description:
WHY: this is the milestone-1 deliverable. It proves the coexistence layer works on a real, hot, load-bearing native component without disturbing the ~hundreds of ICmpPosition call sites across simulation, rendering and AI code.

WHAT:
- Move CCmpPosition state into the entt storage structs from the audit task, accessed through the EnTT component helper. The class keeps deriving from ICmpPosition, keeps DEFAULT_COMPONENT_ALLOCATOR-style per-entity allocation, and keeps its ClassInit subscriptions (MT_TurnStart, MT_TerrainChanged, MT_WaterChanged, MT_Deserialized) plus the existing dynamic MT_Interpolate subscription via DynamicSubscriptionNonsync.
- Serialize/Deserialize must emit and consume exactly the same fields in exactly the same order as today. The serialization version (IComponent::GetSerializationVersion) must not need bumping; if you believe it does, stop and escalate, because that means the format changed.
- No public ICmpPosition signature changes, so no caller changes. Any caller diff is a red flag that state semantics drifted.
- Preserve the special cases in the existing implementation: the turret parent/child relationships, the !m_InWorld "undefined junk" coordinates, and the interpolation state that must survive a Deserialize by being recomputed rather than loaded.

description:
WHY: CCmpPosition (source/simulation2/components/CCmpPosition.cpp) mixes three categories of state in one class, and the port must not accidentally serialize or fail to serialize any of them. This audit is a paper exercise that de-risks the actual port and produces the struct layout the rest of the feature builds on.

WHAT: enumerate every member and classify it:
- Template/static state set from the XML schema in Init: m_AnchorType, m_Floating, m_FloatDepth, m_RotYSpeed.
- Dynamic serialized state: m_InWorld, m_X/m_Z, m_LastX/m_LastZ, m_PrevX/m_PrevZ, m_Y, m_LastYDifference, m_RelativeToGround, m_ConstructionProgress, m_RotX/m_RotY/m_RotZ, m_TurretParent, m_TurretPosition, m_Turrets (std::set<entity_id_t>).
- Explicitly not serialized: m_ActorAnchorType, m_InterpolatedRotX/Y/Z, m_LastInterpolatedRotX/Z, m_ActorFloating, m_EnabledMessageInterpolate.
Then define the entt component structs, keeping the three categories separate per the coexistence-layer convention. Flag the awkward members explicitly: m_Turrets is a heap-allocating std::set inside what should be dense storage (decide whether it stays inline, moves to a side table, or is a separate sparse entt component present only on entities that actually have turrets), and note that the existing Serialize/Deserialize implementation and its exact field order must be reproduced unchanged.

title: EnTT coexistence layer for native IComponent types
description:
WHY: before any component can be migrated, there must be a reusable, determinism-safe mechanism for a native C++ component to keep its IComponent identity (so QueryInterface, CEntityHandle component caches, message subscriptions, and serialization all keep working) while its actual state lives in an entt::registry. Without this layer, each port would reinvent entity mapping and lifecycle handling, and each would be a fresh determinism risk.

WHAT: build the infrastructure only - no gameplay component is ported here.
- A single simulation-owned entt::registry with a defined lifetime tied to CSimContext / CComponentManager (created, reset by ResetState, torn down with the sim).
- A bidirectional entity_id_t <-> entt::entity mapping, since entity_id_t is a u32 with tag bits (ENTITY_TAGMASK for local entities, SYSTEM_ENTITY == 1) and is never reused, whereas entt::entity encodes a recycled index+version. These are NOT interchangeable and must not be reinterpret_cast into each other.
- A CRTP/base helper so a component class declares its storage struct(s) and gets registry-backed accessors, with the IComponent proxy object still allocated per entity by DEFAULT_COMPONENT_ALLOCATOR (its address is stored in SEntityComponentCache and must remain stable for the entity lifetime).
- Explicit determinism rules and guard rails.

OUT OF SCOPE: scripted components, removing anything from CComponentManager, changing serialization format.
notes: Priority demoted P1->P2, tracking parent epic bd_0ad-1u1's demotion (see its note): CCmpPosition access measured at 0.2% of total CPU in captures/2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl, no perf urgency shown by capture data.

title: Convert legacy ECS to EnTT
description:
Migrate 0ad simulation2 from the bespoke CComponentManager/IComponent ECS to EnTT (libraries/source/entt, header-only, already wired into premake via build/premake/extern_libs5.lua).

WHY: the legacy system stores each component as a heap-allocated IComponent* in std::map/unordered_map keyed by entity_id_t, which is pointer-chasing, cache-hostile, and offers no way to iterate component data contiguously. EnTT gives dense per-type storage and views, which is a precondition for later data-oriented simulation work.

SCOPE DECISIONS (settled, do not re-litigate):
1. INCREMENTAL COEXISTENCE, not a big-bang rewrite. EnTT and CComponentManager/IComponent coexist long-term. Components migrate one at a time; every migrated component keeps conforming to the IComponent interface (Init/Deinit/HandleMessage/Serialize/Deserialize) and to the existing message subscription system, so the rest of the engine is untouched.
2. JS-SCRIPTED COMPONENTS (CT_Script / CT_ScriptWrapper) ARE OUT OF SCOPE for milestone 1. Only native C++ (CT_Native) components are touched.
3. DETERMINISM IS A HARD CONSTRAINT FROM DAY ONE. 0ad has lockstep multiplayer (TurnManager/NetClientTurnManager, per-turn ComputeStateHash) and replay reproduction (ReplayTurnManager, commands.txt). Any EnTT-backed component must produce bit-identical serialization, state hashes, and simulation results. Nothing about determinism is deferred to "later".

MILESTONE 1 DELIVERABLE: one real, currently-native, non-scripted component (candidate: CCmpPosition) storing its data in an entt::registry while still presenting as an IComponent, plus the reusable coexistence layer that made it possible, plus determinism validation (replay + state hash + save/load).

KEY ARCHITECTURAL ANCHOR (verified in code): CComponentManager::SerializeState / ComputeStateHash / DumpDebugState iterate m_ComponentsByTypeId (std::map<ComponentTypeId, std::map<entity_id_t, IComponent*>>) and call IComponent::Serialize per entity in ascending entity_id order. If a migrated component keeps a per-entity IComponent proxy registered with the manager exactly as today, and only its *storage* moves into the registry, serialization order and bytes are preserved for free. EnTT storage order (swap-and-pop) must therefore never be observable by simulation logic.
notes: Priority demoted P1->P2 per perf-guru review of captures/2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl: all CCmpPosition access is 1.8s of 868s total CPU = 0.2%. This capture gives the EnTT migration no hot-path perf mandate; if P1 is retained it should be justified architecturally, not by perf urgency, since it currently outranks CCmpUnitMotionManager::Push (15.5% of sim wall) and TaskManager wakeup overhead (5.7% of sim wall).

title: Investigate sync-CPU-per-turn cost tradeoff of bd_0ad-t0j clock-hoist fix on lower-core-count machines

title: Query::source can dangle if referenced entity is destroyed while a range query is active
description: Pre-existing TODO found at source/simulation2/components/CCmpRangeManager.cpp ~line 201 during bd_0ad-ea4 investigation: 'this could crash if an entity is destroyed while a Query is still referencing it.' Query::source is presumably a CEntityHandle or similar; if the source entity is destroyed without DestroyActiveQuery being called first, the query would reference a dead entity, current TODO comment implies no runtime enforcement exists yet. Action: verify the actual lifetime-management contract for Query::source (is DestroyActiveQuery guaranteed to run on entity destruction via some message handler?), close the gap if it's real, or add an ENSURE/assertion if it's currently assumed-safe by convention only.

title: Audit CCmpPathfinder unjoined async futures spanning turn boundary
description: Surfaced during bd_0ad-ea4 investigation (principal-engineer review, later determined NOT to be the cause of that bead's reported nondeterminism -- state-hash comparison found no divergence). CCmpPathfinder::StartProcessingMoves dispatches async path-computation work to TaskManager workers and does not join before returning (source/simulation2/components/CCmpPathfinder.cpp ~line 858-870); the futures stay in flight across RunJobs(), MaybeIncrementalGC(), and serialization/state-hash logic in CSimulation2Impl::Update, joined only via SendRequestedPaths() on the NEXT turn (source/simulation2/Simulation2.cpp, dispatch ~line 624, join ~line 560). This is the only genuine main-thread-runs-arbitrary-code-while-workers-still-active window in the sim update. Nothing racy was found on this pass (PathRequests::Compute only reads shared m_LongPathfinder/m_PathfinderHier state during the parallel region; VertexPathfinder instances are per-thread and cleared at end of each call), but the window itself was not exhaustively audited for every possible main-thread mutation during that gap. Action: do a focused audit of everything CSimulation2Impl::Update touches between dispatch and join to positively confirm none of it can mutate pathfinder-shared state, and consider adding a comment documenting the safety argument so this doesn't need to be re-derived by the next investigator (as happened here).

title: EntityData::interfaceMask/componentCache/FlagMasks::Mirage go stale if components change post-creation
description: Surfaced during bd_0ad-ea4 investigation (principal-engineer review). CCmpRangeManager.cpp's EntityData caches (interfaceMask, componentCache, and the Mirage bit in FlagMasks from bd_0ad-ahy.1) are populated ONLY at MT_Create time and recomputed on MT_Deserialized (RepopulateComponentCaches). If any component is ever added to or removed from an already-created entity (e.g. via a dynamic AddComponent-after-construction path, if one exists or is added in future), TestEntityQuery's fast-path bitmask/cache checks would silently return stale (wrong) answers instead of the correct live QueryInterface result. Currently believed safe because all AddComponent calls happen in ConstructEntity before CMessageCreate is sent (no post-construction dynamic add path found), but this is an implicit invariant that isn't enforced or asserted anywhere. Action: either add an ENSURE/assertion that catches any post-creation component add/remove and recomputes the caches, or add a code comment + regression test documenting the invariant so a future change can't silently reintroduce a correctness bug here.

Next steps: after the bd_0ad-bzj fix has been in use for a while (e.g. during bd_0ad-093 CPU-utilization epic replay-hash validation work), watch for recurrence of segfaults during -ooslog replay runs. If it recurs, bisect further (may be non-deterministic or state-dependent). If it does not recur after reasonable exercise of the replay path, this bead can likely be closed as resolved-by-bzj.

title: Phase 5: P/E-core-aware GetParallelWidth() (fix oversubscription)
description:
Deliberately last mandatory phase - its value only measurable once a real parallel region exists (Phase 4b), and its correct default depends on that regions shape.

- Add Threading::GetCpuTopology() helper (source/ps/Threading.h, already included by TaskManager.cpp:25). Windows: GetLogicalProcessorInformationEx(RelationProcessorCore,...), count cores at max EfficiencyClass. Linux: check /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuN/cpu_capacity or cpufreq/cpuinfo_max_freq. macOS: hw.perflevel0.logicalcpu. Fallback: hardware_concurrency() on any failure or non-hybrid system - must never be worse than current behavior.
- Decouple pool size from parallel-region participant count: keep GetNumberOfWorkers() unchanged (pool size, still used e.g. by CCmpPathfinder.cpp:91-94,99 to size per-thread arrays). Add new TaskManager::GetParallelWidth(), defaulting to detected performance-core count (8 on the profiled Arrowlake-S), overridable via config key taskmanager.parallelwidth. ParallelFor caps participants at GetParallelWidth()-1 (main thread is the plus-one).
- Do NOT set hard thread affinity masks (defeats Windows 11 Thread Director P/E steering, breaks on VM/restricted cpuset, non-reproducible across SKU variants with different E-core counts). SetThreadIdealProcessor (a hint) on workers is acceptable only if measurement justifies it - not part of baseline plan.
- Sweep parallelwidth in 4,6,8,12,16,24 on the stress benchmark and pick the shipped default from data, not theory. Verify fallback path on a non-hybrid machine and a restricted cpuset/container if available.

Files: source/ps/Threading.h/.cpp, source/ps/TaskManager.cpp (:53-57), config schema.
acceptance_criteria: Topology detection verified with sane fallback on non-hybrid/failure cases. Default parallelwidth chosen from sweep data and documented. VTune-measured preemption wait significantly reduced versus Phase 4b baseline.

title: Investigate EntityData 40->56 byte growth impact on EntityMap stride/hot lookup (bd_0ad-117 follow-up)
description:
WHY: bd_0ad-117 added a 128-bit interfaceMask (u64[2]) to CCmpRangeManager::EntityData to eliminate a componentCache pointer-chase in TestEntityQuery, growing sizeof(EntityData) from 40 to 56 bytes (static_assert updated at CCmpRangeManager.cpp:297). perf-guru flagged this widens the EntityMap<EntityData> stride (EntityMap.h value_type = {u32 first; EntityData second}), which could add memory-bandwidth/cache pressure to the already-hot m_EntityData.find(id)/visitor(id) lookup inside ForEachInRange (89.59s exclusive, 86.7% of which is that lookup line, in the pre-bd_0ad-117 baseline capture 2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl).

WHAT: Capture a post-bd_0ad-117 Superluminal profile (command: SuperluminalCmd.exe run windows --freq 8190 --max-duration 180 --resolve --use-new-pdb-parser --allow-overwrite --capture-path captures\bd_0ad-117_postfix_interfacemask.etl --working-dir binaries\system binaries\system\pyrogenesis.exe -autostart=scenarios/combat_demo_huge -autostart-nonvisual -autostart-player=-1 -autostart-speed=20 -autostart-victory=endless -autostart-disable-replay -autostart-seed=0 -autostart-aiseed=0 — requires an elevated/admin shell, which was unavailable when bd_0ad-117 closed) and compare ForEachInRange<lambda_2> exclusive cost against the 89.59s baseline. If it rose materially, the componentCache pointer-chase win was partly offset by wider per-candidate iteration cost.

If confirmed, the fix direction (per perf-guru) is to move interfaceMask out of the hot EntityData record into a parallel SoA array (u64[2] per slot) indexed by the same subdivision-array index used for EntityData, rather than fattening the per-entity record that's randomly accessed by id on every ForEachInRange visit.

Note: the 128-bit width itself is NOT negotiable/reducible — code-explorer confirmed script-registered interfaces (public mod, via Engine.RegisterInterface) push real interface IDs up to 113 (49 native + 64 script, ComponentManager.cpp Script_RegisterInterface shares one counter with native TypeList.h registration), so a 64-bit mask would silently break queries for real gameplay interfaces in the 50-113 ID range. Any fix here must preserve full 128-bit coverage, just relocate it out of the hot struct if warranted.
notes:
Post-fix capture reviewed (captures/2026-09-09_12-43-09_pyrogenesis.etl vs baseline captures/2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl) by perf-guru. Verdict: unresolved, not confirmed and not clearable.

The originally proposed canary, ForEachInRange<lambda_2> exclusive, is NOT usable: it rose +8.4% (89.59s -> 97.10s) but this is confounded - TestEntityQuery's TotalCallCount dropped 40.2% post-fix (1.485M -> 888,475) while PerformQuery/lambda_2 call counts only moved ~7%, indicating MSVC partially inlined the now-smaller TestEntityQuery into lambda_2's visitor at many call sites. That shifts attributed cost from TestEntityQuery into lambda_2 without changing total work, so lambda_2's delta cannot arbitrate the stride-regression question.

Two signals point in opposite directions:
- AGAINST the stride-regression concern: aggregate PerformQuery per-call time improved -7.6% (71.59us -> 66.13us). If wider EntityData/EntityMap stride were meaningfully hurting m_EntityData.find(id) traffic, this aggregate (which is immune to the inlining reshuffle) would not have improved.
- FOR the concern: ForEachInRange<lambda_1> exclusive rose +18.1% (17.76s -> 20.97s) on ~7% FEWER calls (~+27% per call). lambda_1 does much less TestEntityQuery work than lambda_2 so it should absorb far less inlining-driven reshuffle, yet it regressed proportionally more - this looks like a genuine stride/cache-pressure signal rather than attribution shift.

RETARGET: use ForEachInRange<lambda_1> (the parabolic-branch visitor) as the clean probe for this investigation instead of lambda_2, which is too polluted by the inlining confound to arbitrate. Keep at P3 - the aggregate win from bd_0ad-117 is real and 20.97s of lambda_1 is a small slice of PerformQuery's 171.75s total.

If a clean, inlining-proof measurement is ever needed (isolates true stride effect from the inlining artifact): rebuild with __declspec(noinline) on CCmpRangeManager::TestEntityQuery for both arms and recapture, which pins TestEntityQuery's call count at ~1.485M.

title: Early LOGMESSAGE calls before FileLogger init are silently swallowed
description: During startup, EarlyInit() (source/main.cpp) initializes CProfiler2 (and now Superluminal::Initialise() via bd_0ad-5g5) before the FileLogger is created in RunGameOrAtlas() (source/main.cpp ~line 693, after InitVfs()). This likely affects other early-startup LOGMESSAGE calls too, not just Superluminal's. Consider buffering early log messages and flushing once FileLogger attaches, or creating a minimal stderr/console logger earlier in startup.

title: Widen TaskBatch scope across per-turn ExecuteActiveQueries invocations
description: Follow-up from bd_0ad-92h post-fix perf-guru validation (capture 2026-09-08_16-51-24 vs 2026-09-08_16-14-24 baseline). The bd_0ad-92h fix batches the ~23 Future pushes within a single CCmpRangeManager::ExecuteActiveQueries call under one TaskBatch/PushTasks flush. However ExecuteActiveQueries itself is invoked ~7.9x per turn (186,311 calls / 23,649 turns), so PushTasks/notify_all is still called ~7.07 times per turn (167,220 calls, ~113us each = ~0.80ms/turn, 10.8% of main-thread turn time in the AFTER capture). Widening TaskBatch scope so all per-turn ExecuteActiveQueries invocations share one flush would cut this to roughly 1x per turn (~0.11ms/turn), a further ~7x reduction in wake overhead. Note: PushTasks already implements a numTasks>=workerCount ? notify_all : notify_one-per-task threshold (source/ps/TaskManager.cpp), so no further change needed there -- this bead is specifically about hoisting/sharing the TaskBatch instance across sibling ExecuteActiveQueries calls within the same turn. Files: source/simulation2/components/CCmpRangeManager.cpp (ExecuteActiveQueries call sites), source/ps/TaskManager.h/.cpp (TaskBatch).

All tests are passing.
Profiling command was provided to user to validate positive performance impact.
close_reason: won't-fix: invalid premise. principal-engineer analysis confirms the ~7.9 ExecuteActiveQueries-calls/turn figure is an artifact of TurnManager's fast-forward loop under autostart-speed=20 (7-8 distinct simulation turns per rendered frame), not repeated invocations within a single turn -- at normal 1x speed there is exactly one call per turn. Sharing a TaskBatch across turns is also unsafe: ExecuteActiveQueries's worker tasks read/write m_EntityData and query.lastMatch, and PostMessage(RangeUpdate) at the end of each call feeds JS OnRangeUpdate handlers (UnitAI/BuildingAI/Auras/Gate/TriggerPoint) whose effects are visible before the same turn's MotionFormation/MotionUnit/Final phases and before the next turn -- deferring flush+Get across turns would race and break determinism/replay. Additionally numFutures already == workerCount in practice, so PushTasks already takes the single notify_all path per call (bd_0ad-92h captured the full available win here). Remaining wake-latency cost is already tracked as bd_0ad-jto (spin-then-sleep workers), which is the correct, determinism-neutral place to pursue further gains.

title: Reserve/bulk-append subdivisionResultsBuffer in FastSpatialSubdivision::GetNear
description: Follow-up from bd_0ad-ahy Superluminal validation (capture 2026-09-08_15-34-43_pyrogenesis). vector<uint32_t>::_Insert_counted_range is 25.3s exclusive (~3.9% of total thread running time) in GetNear's result-buffer append path. subdivisionResultsBuffer is already reused across calls (not allocation churn), so this is per-call insert cost. Reserve to a high-water mark, or switch to a bulk/memcpy-style append, to reduce it.
notes: Closed as subsumed by bd_0ad-v2l. GetNear is a 3-line pass-through to GetInRange (Spatial.h ~565-571), so it has no fix of its own. reserve() is also the wrong remedy: the per-worker result buffers are already reused across calls with no reallocation churn; the measured cost is the bulk out.insert(...) copy itself (88.7% of GetInRange's own time per Superluminal). Real fix is the ForEachInRange/ForEachNear visitor redesign landing under v2l.

title: Assertion dialogs still possible in -archivebuild and other InitVfs-skipping CLI paths
description: WHY: while fixing bd_0ad-5zm (assertions triggering a blocking GUI dialog in headless mode), found that main.cpp's RunGameOrAtlas() has multiple early-return code paths that skip InitVfs() (the only place that normally registers the psDisplayError app hook). We explicitly fixed the isNonVisualReplay (-replay=<path>) path by registering the hook there too, but did not audit/fix other paths that also return early before InitVfs (e.g. -archivebuild, and possibly the 'version' branch, Atlas invocation, etc.). Any assertion/ENSURE failure hit during those paths would still fall through to the library default def_display_error() (source/lib/app_hooks.cpp) which always returns ERI_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, causing a modal dialog that would hang an unattended/scripted invocation.\n\nWHAT: audit every early-return branch in main.cpp::RunGameOrAtlas (and any other entry point) that runs before InitVfs(args) is reached, and either register the display_error hook explicitly (mirroring the isNonVisualReplay fix) for genuinely non-interactive paths, or confirm the path is always interactive and does not need it.

title: Update ADR-001 Appendix A with corrected 3-pool split cost measurement
description:
WHY: bd_0ad-5ki re-measured the Template/State/Derived 3-way pool split cost using CCmpPosition-sized (128-132B) structs and found the real penalty is ~1.05-1.6x (creation order) / ~1.66-1.85x (shuffled) / ~1.25-1.4x (25% density) at practical N -- materially lower than the ~2.2-2.5x figure the original ADR-001 Appendix A decision was informed by (measured with undersized 8-12 byte structs). Also note the caveat from perf-guru's final review: the measurement has all three pools populated in identical creation order (best-case dense-array alignment for a split); real components will diverge, so 1.5-1.7x should be treated as a floor, not a ceiling.

WHAT: update ADR-001 Appendix A's rationale/numbers section to cite the corrected bd_0ad-5ki figures instead of (or alongside, marked superseded) the bd_0ad-1u1.1.6 figures, and add the alignment-bias caveat so future readers don't treat 1.5-1.7x as a hard ceiling.

title: Measure CCmpPosition port performance impact (before/after)
description:
WHY: the whole point of the EnTT migration is data layout and iteration cost. Milestone 1 is small enough that it may show no win, or even a small regression from the extra indirection through the registry - it is important to know which, before committing to migrating dozens more components on the assumption that it pays off. Google Benchmark and the benchmarks target are already wired up (libraries/source/benchmark, binaries/system/benchmarks.exe) and currently unused by simulation2.

WHAT:
- Add a benchmark exercising the realistic access patterns: per-entity ICmpPosition::GetPosition2D/MoveTo-style calls over a few thousand entities, plus the MT_TurnStart broadcast path, plus the MT_Interpolate path.
- Measure the pre-port and post-port builds and record numbers on this issue.
- Also capture a coarse whole-game signal (replay wall-clock time and/or Tracy capture of the simulation frame) since the microbenchmark may not reflect real cache behaviour.
- Report honestly: if the port is neutral or slightly slower at this stage, say so and note what would need to change (batch iteration replacing per-entity virtual calls) to realise the win.
acceptance_criteria: Before/after numbers for both the microbenchmark and a whole-replay run are recorded on this issue, with an explicit statement of whether milestone 1 is a perf win, neutral, or a regression, and why.
notes: Priority demoted P2->P3 per perf-guru review: measuring a component (CCmpPosition) that is 0.2% of total CPU per captures/2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl; any before/after delta will be inside run-to-run noise, especially given bd_0ad-ea4's unresolved non-determinism.

title: Worker threads show as bare TIDs in Tracy
description: Tracy never receives thread names for worker threads because debug_SetThreadName (source/lib/sysdep/os/win/wdbg.cpp) early-returns unless a debugger is attached. Add a tracy::SetThreadName() call in source/ps/TaskManager.cpp (around where worker threads are spawned, ~line 253) so worker threads are labeled in the Tracy profiler instead of showing as bare TIDs.
design: Added tracy::SetThreadName(name.c_str()) call in WorkerThread::RunUntilDeath() (source/ps/TaskManager.cpp), right after the existing debug_SetThreadName() call and before g_Profiler2.RegisterCurrentThread(). Also added #include <tracy/Tracy.hpp>. This runs on the worker thread itself (called from within RunUntilDeath, the thread's own entry point), giving each worker a unique name like 'Task Mgr #N' visible in Tracy regardless of whether a debugger is attached. Verified source/ps/TaskManager.cpp compiles cleanly (isolated engine.vcxproj rebuild of TaskManager.obj succeeded with no errors); full solution build currently fails for unrelated pre-existing reasons (in-progress EnTT conversion work on this branch missing 'entt' in premake extern_libs for engine/gui/graphics projects) - not caused by or related to this change.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: tracy::SetThreadName() added to TaskManager.cpp worker thread entry point; TaskManager.cpp compiles cleanly in isolation.

title: FrameMark bisects the top-level PROFILE2 frame zone in Tracy timeline
description: FrameMark is called at the end of Frame()/NonVisualFrame() in main.cpp, but it falls inside the still-open PROFILE2("frame") zone entered earlier in the loop iteration. This means the frame boundary marker bisects the top-level zone in the Tracy timeline instead of aligning cleanly with it. Cosmetic trace-alignment issue; fixing it requires restructuring the scope of that top-level PROFILE2("frame") zone so it closes before FrameMark fires.
design: Wrapped the body of Frame() and NonVisualFrame() in source/main.cpp in a nested block scope containing the PROFILE2("frame") RAII guard (and the rest of the per-frame work), so the guard's destructor fires and closes the Tracy zone before the trailing FrameMark; call is reached. FrameMark; now sits just outside that block, after the zone has closed, instead of inside it. No frame logic/behavior changed; early-return paths (e.g. on shutdown) still skip FrameMark exactly as before, since the return still exits the enclosing function during stack unwind of the nested block.
close_reason: Restructured PROFILE2("frame") zone scope in source/main.cpp so it closes before FrameMark fires in both Frame() and NonVisualFrame(); cosmetic Tracy alignment fix, no behavior change.

title: Investigate TaskManager worker spin-then-sleep as a fresh, properly-methodologized effort
description:
Deferred/abandoned in bd_0ad-093.2 after 7 rounds of single-run-measurement spin-tuning attempts (adaptive EWMA x3, fixed-iteration, calibrated-fixed x2) proved unable to reliably outperform a plain blocking condition_variable::wait -- throughput ranged from -7.1% to +11.2% vs baseline across variants with no run-to-run reproducibility, and the one seemingly-best variant (an accidental ~30-38us pinned spin, +11.2% stress throughput) could not be reliably reproduced by deliberate design (calibrated versions targeting the same width undershot due to idle-vs-loaded PAUSE cost differing ~2x on the test machine).

If revisited, this needs real methodology, not more one-shot tuning:
- 3-5 runs per configuration minimum, report medians and spread, not single samples
- Any calibration must account for load-dependent PAUSE cost (idle-machine calibration undermeasures loaded-machine PAUSE latency by ~2x on the reference hardware -- see full measurement history in bd_0ad-0rp's closed comments)
- Consider whether a stress-scenario-only or per-workload-class spin budget makes more sense than a single one-size-fits-all constant, since the two test scenarios (saturated stress vs moderate/intermittent) pulled the optimal width in opposite directions
- The baseline to beat is the plain blocking wait (current shipped state) -- reference measurement: baseline stress-scenario throughput 19,314 turns in a matched 2-17s combat_demo_huge window, sync CPU/turn 0.0887ms.

Low priority / no urgency -- current shipped behavior (plain blocking wait) is a known-good, zero-risk baseline. This is speculative future optimization work only.

title: Re-check original PerformQuery-count profiler signal from bd_0ad-ea4 against current HEAD
description: bd_0ad-ea4 (combat_demo_huge nonvisual speed=20 apparent nondeterminism) was closed as non-reproducible: two independent runs of a freshly-verified-clean Release build produced byte-identical per-turn state hashes across 3000 turns via the canonical -ooslog gate. However, the ORIGINAL evidence for that bead was different and indirect: PerformQuery call-count deltas observed between two Superluminal profiler captures of the same workload/binary/seed (e.g. 1,090,657 vs 1,066,013 calls at turn 19617, -2.3%). That specific measurement was not directly re-attempted against current HEAD -- only the state-hash-based check was redone. It's possible the call-count signal was itself a profiling-capture-overhead artifact unrelated to true state divergence (plausible, since exhaustive state-hash comparison found none), but this hasn't been positively confirmed. Action: take two fresh Superluminal captures of the same combat_demo_huge/speed=20 workload and check whether PerformQuery/other call counts still diverge at matching turns despite state hashes matching; if they do diverge, that would indicate the call-count metric itself is not a reliable state-divergence signal (worth documenting for future profiling comparisons per the bd_0ad-ahy.1/bd_0ad-093.8 measurement-hazard notes), rather than reopening bd_0ad-ea4 as a correctness bug.

title: VertexPathfinder::Vertex struct lacks default member initializers (code hygiene)
description: Surfaced during bd_0ad-ea4 investigation. source/simulation2/helpers/VertexPathfinder.cpp ~line 643: 'Vertex vert;' creates an uninitialized Vertex struct, with only status/quadInward/quadOutward explicitly set afterward (lines ~644-646). title: Phase 6 (optional/measurement-gated): m_UnitShapes container, BroadcastMessage parallelization, range/motion overlap
description:
Optional follow-ups, each independently gated on re-measurement after Phase 5. Do not implement speculatively.

1. m_UnitShapes dense container: CCmpObstructionManager.cpp:158-162 std::map<u32,UnitShape> operator[] cost - only pursue if Phase 1s SetMovingFlag early-out did not already remove the cost on re-measurement. Broader change: map is iterated in key order at :284 and :1390 (subdivision rebuild, debug render) - a vector/free-list replacement must preserve ascending-index iteration and handle holes.
2. Parallelizing CComponentManager::BroadcastMessage (roughly 11.4s/180s in Sim - Update Start, e.g. CCmpPosition::HandleMessage). Requires proving per-message-type handler independence - blanket parallelization is a determinism minefield. Scope to a per-message-type opt-in allowlist, or skip if audit shows insufficient independent handlers.
3. Overlapping CCmpRangeManager query execution with motion (range results consumed via PostMessage at CCmpRangeManager.cpp:1345-1348, currently after motion). High value, high risk: PerformQuery reads entity positions which PostMove writes in the same turn - the two regions DO alias. Would require a read-only position snapshot taken at turn start. Needs its own design doc before implementation; do not attempt before Phase 5 is stable.
4. Work-stealing deques for TaskManager queue (replacing single global mutex+deque): explicitly NOT recommended by the architecture review - VTune shows spin/overhead time is 0.046s (negligible), so the mutex is not the bottleneck; ParallelFors atomic-cursor design already reduces lock acquisitions from roughly one per task (3.86M) to roughly one per participant per region. Re-open ONLY if post-Phase-4b/5 profiling shows PopTask lock time as a top-5 cost (predicted it will not be).
acceptance_criteria: Each sub-item independently evaluated against post-Phase-5 profiling data; implement only those that show measurable benefit. Work-stealing deque item may be closed as wont-fix if profiling confirms prediction.

title: Demote ENSURE(it != m_EntityData.end()) in PerformQuery inner loop to debug-only
description: Follow-up from bd_0ad-ahy Superluminal validation (capture 2026-09-08_15-34-43_pyrogenesis). The ENSURE in CCmpRangeManager::PerformQuery's inner candidate loop costs ~4.4s exclusive (~1.0% of total thread running time) checking an invariant that FastSpatialSubdivision already guarantees (that ids returned by GetNear are present in m_EntityData). title: Store index into EntityData in subdivision to skip m_EntityData.find in PerformQuery
description: Follow-up from bd_0ad-ahy Superluminal validation (capture 2026-09-08_15-34-43_pyrogenesis). After the ahy interface-cache hoist, m_EntityData.find(subdivisionResultsBuffer[i]) in CCmpRangeManager::PerformQuery is now the top remaining indirection in the candidate loop (~15s exclusive, ~2.3% of total thread running time in the profiled workload). Note: bd_0ad-6uw grew EntityData (added cached y), so each find now touches a slightly larger record than baseline -- did not hurt in this measurement but worth watching if EntityData grows further.
notes: STALE PREMISE flagged by perf-guru review of captures/2026-09-09_11-09-12_pyrogenesis.etl: EntityMap::find is already O(1) direct-index access (EntityMap.h:229), not a search — as written this bead would produce a no-op patch. The real cost perf-guru found in the same area is the cache miss on the sparse EntityData record accessed via the visitor body (77.7s = 86.7% of ForEachInRange's 89.6s exclusive, ~9% of all CPU) — recommend either closing this bead and filing a new one for 'store hot query fields (x, z, ownerMask, flags, size) SoA directly in subdivision bins' at P1, or rewriting this bead's WHAT section to that effect. title: Consider pointing entt include path at single_include amalgamated header for faster builds
description: WHY: discovered by perf-guru during review of bd_0ad-5je (entt Windows include path fix). The entt submodule ships a pre-amalgamated libraries/source/entt/entt/single_include/entt/entt.hpp in addition to the split libraries/source/entt/entt/src/entt tree that extern_libs5.lua now points at. Pointing the premake include path at single_include instead of src would cut preprocessor file-open churn across the ~10 projects that transitively pull in entt via ComponentManager.h. This is a build-time-only optimization with zero runtime/behavioral effect, but it does change which literal files get compiled, so it was deliberately kept out of bd_0ad-5je (which was scoped purely to fixing Windows include-path reproducibility, not changing which entt distribution form is used). Speculative/optional -- only worth doing if build times become a complaint.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) switch extern_libs5.lua's entt add_header_only_source_include_paths call to point at entt/single_include and confirm build times improve and all consumers still compile cleanly, or (b) close as won't-do if build-time impact is judged negligible.
